News.title: Huge fire by railway tracks halts trains to UK’s busiest station as motorists engulfed in thick smoke on major motorway
News.content:
BLAZE CHAOS Huge fire by railway tracks halts trains to UK’s busiest station as motorists engulfed in thick smoke on major motorway

A HUGE fire by railway tracks has halted all services to the UK’s busiest train station and left motorists engulfed in smoke on the M25.

Crews from Essex County Fire and Rescue Service are currently tackling the blaze next to the tracks in Waltham Cross, Hertfordshire, which has sparked chaos at London Liverpool Street station.



Trains running to and from Liverpool Street have been stopped as a result of the blaze.

All Greater Anglia services towards the major transport hub are currently being diverted via Seven Sisters, a spokesperson confirmed.



Thick plumes of smoke visible for miles triggered at least 50 emergency calls at around 2pm after the blaze broke out close to the M25.

Drivers are being warned to take extra care on the major motorway between junctions 25 (Enfield) and 26 (Waltham Abbey).



Greater Anglia said the London Fire Brigade requested trains were stopped because of multiple fires close to the railway lines.

Services to and from Stansted Airport in Essex, Cambridge North, Meridian Water in Hertfordshire and Hertford East have also all been affected.

Smoke from the fire is said to be affecting visibility on the carriageway.

Rail operators warned that significant disruption across the network is expected to continue until further notice.



A spokesperson for Greater Anglia said: “Unfortunately, we have received reports of multiple fires close to the railway lines and as a result, and a safety precaution, the London Fire Brigade have instructed that all train movements in the area be stopped.”

Stansted Express journeys are also being significantly affected, with estimated travel times of up to two hours and 30 minutes.

Passengers travelling from London Liverpool Street to the airport are advised to take Underground services to Kings Cross St Pancras, board a Great Northern train to Cambridge, and then transfer to a train to Stansted Airport.

A Stansted Express spokesperson said: “Train services running through this station may be delayed or diverted via Seven Sisters. Disruption is expected until further notice.

“Unfortunately, we have received reports of multiple fires close to the railway lines and as a result, and a safety precaution, the London Fire Brigade have instructed that all train movements in the area be stopped.



“In reaction trains towards and from Liverpool Street will be diverted via Seven Sisters until further notice.

“Network Rail and the emergency response team are on site working as quickly as possible to put out the fires and restore the train service to normal.”

Alternative travel options are in place for affected passengers.

Greater Anglia tickets are being accepted on London Underground services, as well as on Great Northern, Thameslink, London Buses, and London Overground routes.

Passengers travelling between Stratford and Hertford East may use services via Liverpool Street or the Central Line on the Underground.



An LFB spokesman said: “One of the Brigade’s Terrain Support Vehicles has been sent to the scene to support firefighting efforts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The vehicle provides off-road capability enabling the transportation of additional equipment closer to fires on open ground.

“Each vehicle carries approximately 475 litres of water, a backpack blower, ear defenders, beaters and misting lance technology, which allows firefighters to pump water and drive, enabling them to tackle grass fires more quickly and safely.”

News.title: Our city’s failing working class kids – it’s easier for teens to join a gang and make money from crime than get a job
News.content:
NO HOPE Our city’s failing working class kids – it’s easier for teens to join a gang and make money from crime than get a job

“THERE’S just not a lot of hope left around here,” says Kelsey Percival, rocking her buggy to settle her five-week-old baby boy.

The 21-year-old first time mum’s worries go beyond those of her little one’s sleep, or milk intake, as the pair live in an area which has the worst opportunities for working class children in the whole of England.



Newcastle Central and West is a vast locality which is home to the city’s iconic quayside, famous Tyne Bridge, Castle Keep and upmarket bars and restaurants.

However, it also includes a large residential area, taking in Blakelaw, Westerhope, Lemington, Fenham, Chapel House, Elswick, Scotswood and Benwell.



And the figures are stark.

If you are a white British child eligible for free school meals and live here, you can expect to earn just £13,734 by the age of 28.

According to the report by educational charity the Sutton Trust, a mere 35 per cent of young people over the age of 16 in this demographic are in education or work at all.

Meanwhile, only six per cent will complete a degree by the age of 22, and the area has been ranked bottom out of 543 constituencies for social mobility and outcomes for white British children.

Residents tell us it’s easier for young people to make money from crime than it is to get a job, and the city is plagued by gang warfare.

In Blakelaw, branches of Greggs and Farmfoods are doing a roaring trade during the lunchtime rush at the rundown Binswood Avenue shopping precinct, where a cash machine has been ripped out of a wall.



We spoke to Kelsey and her friend Brooke Hull, 21, who believe Newcastle’s west end and its children are being overlooked in favour of kids in London.

Brooke, a foster carer, said: “There is knife crime, and you hear about people getting raped which is scary as a young girl.

“Raising kids, there just isn’t a lot to do. You’re always looking behind you when you walk down the street with your child.



“Kids used to play outside but now they are getting arrested for stabbings and robberies.

“I see children on bikes all the time – the other day I was almost wiped out by an e-bike. It’s shocking.

“I only hope by the time my little girl is older there are parks for her to go to and community centres and help to get a job.

“But there is a tight knit sense of community. We watch out for each other.”

Kelsey, a stay-at-home mum, added: “It’s really hard to get work. Everything is closing down. There should be more groups for teenagers and help for them get jobs.



“There’s just not a lot of hope left around here. Parents are doing their best, but mums are scared to let their kids go out.

“The government focuses on funding for places like London but when it comes to the North East they lose interest. The west end of Newcastle has been left behind and kids are being failed.”

The multicultural West Road cuts directly through the constituency and is a melting pot of South Asian, Middle Eastern and fast food restaurants, which sit alongside betting shops and international grocery stores.

Chloe Foley, 23, who lives close by, said: “It was a lovely area when I was growing up but over the past ten years it has gone downhill.

“There is litter everywhere, pouring out of bins, rats too. I think the environment has a huge impact on young people growing up around here. There is gang violence based off postcodes and they are all against each other.



“Kids are being brought up to think that crime is okay and aren’t being supported to go to school. When I was a child, I used to play out with no worries. Now I have a little girl and I’d never let her out on her own.”

In November 2022, 14-year-old Gordon Gault was stabbed to death with a machete after vying groups from Benwell and Elswick made derogatory rap videos about each another.

Carlos Neto and Lawson Netty, both 18, were found guilty of his manslaughter and jailed for nine years and two months and two years and eight months respectively. They were also convicted of unlawful wounding in relation to a second victim.



Chloe, a supervisor at a card shop, added: “I can’t even get off the bus without feeling scared. I was followed up the street while on my way to work the other day.

“I once saw someone getting mugged on a street corner, in broad daylight. There are a lot of drug dealers around here, young boys who are still in school. They are already on that pathway – all they need is work.”

For decades, Scotswood, Benwell and Elswick were fuelled by the mighty Elswick Works – one of the largest engineering complexes in the world.

The entire area was built around the factory, from its founding in 1847, until its closure in 1979.

Locomotives, tanks, bridges, warships and naval guns were among the industrial products manufactured at the plant, and terraced houses were built to accommodate tens of thousands of workers.



But with decline of industry came unemployment, the closure of shops and pubs, empty homes and a concentration of poverty.

Much of the area falls within the most deprived ten per cent nationally.

Cleaner Maisie Mitchell, 35, said: “Kids are being left behind here.

“Around here, the local park gets vandalised, kids drink alcohol and take drugs. They come out of school and fall into crime as they see no benefit in working.

“They are just sponging. There are issues with prostitution and drug dealers everywhere.”



Louise Hood, a 48-year-old office worker, added: “There aren’t a lot of opportunities here for kids.

“I am not shocked that so many teenagers are out of work. Most of the 16-year-olds close to where I live are hooligans.

“They are into crime and drugs. That’s how a lot of them get their money. I have two adult kids and they are both in work.



“My son is 20 and he didn’t start work until he was 19. He went to college for a while and he was out of work for a year, because he couldn’t get a job.

“You see a lot of young people not really doing much, just hanging around on motorbikes, and in the parks. It’s such a waste.”

Sofia Bowers, 19, grew up in the area, but is now a student of history and war at York University.

She said: “I am not massively shocked by the data even though I am at uni, and my sister went to Cambridge. It’s the kind of thing that can happen when you’re not encouraged by your parents.

“I don’t feel as safe here as I do in York. There are a lot of gangs. There used to be a youth club, but it was stopped, and that probably hasn’t helped.



“There’s not much community. You see a lot of people in their early 20s hanging round not really doing much.

“I think there should be more going on in the community to help them.”

Rebecca and Lisa, who didn’t want to give their full names, work together in the area.

Rebecca said: “If young people are not in work or education, they’re stealing or selling drugs.



“That’s more attractive to them because of the money. They can stay in bed all day and go out on a night time and make a bit of money.

“It’s really shocking, but I think that’s what a lot of kids naturally fall into. There is nothing to push them in the right direction. There aren’t many jobs here.

“I have a 13-year-old and I worry about her future, because I feel like kids follow in each other’s footsteps.

“The wage of less than £14K for a 28-year-old is terrible, and you can understand why kids resort to crime.



“Your wages don’t cover a lot due to the cost of living.”

Lisa added: “Teachers have no control. There’s no discipline. They’re not to blame, I think their hands are tied.

“Kids are running wild as a result. There should be more youth centres and things for young people to do. There’s nothing here.”

Nichola Wright, 58, who works in sales, added: “There is bias towards certain groups of people.

“If you are white and young here, you will be overlooked in favour of someone else. I do think people from ethnic minorities push their kids more in terms of education.



“In other countries, they don’t have the same opportunities. They have to do their homework, and they can’t go on their phones. They’re very strict about it.”

Her friend Sonia Hamilton, a 56-year-old self employed cleaner, said: “There is bias towards certain groups of people.

“A lot of white parents are young people having kids. Kids having kids. They know how to work the system to get benefits.



“You get more money than you do if you work. There is a definite lack of respect.

“Kids from ethnic minorities are taught more respect. It’s in their culture. My kids both work, they’ve followed my lead and their dads’.

“But a lot of young people think, ‘Why should I work?’ And there’s a lack of role models.”

Pat Nicholl volunteers at Newcastle Food Bank based at Venerable Bede Church.

“It is really difficult for young people to get opportunities,” the 73-year-old said.



“When I was a kid, you could walk into a job on a Saturday but now, even for the most menial of jobs, you need a CV. We are stopping young people from getting jobs as we are putting too many obstacles in their way.

“I think we have neglected them for a long time.”

But Scott Philipson, a 27-year-old mechanic from Cowgate and dad to Freddie, three, disagreed.

He said: “I do think it is a lot harder for young people to get jobs – but if you put your head down, you can get anywhere in life. If you want something, go out and work for it.

“I don’t think kids nowadays have any drive. They are lazy.”



To help solve the issues in the area, The Sutton Trust says non-specific “16-19 initiatives” should be put in place.

It also argues the National Funding Formula should be reformed to help target the most disadvantaged areas, such as Newcastle’s west end.

Chi Onwurah, Labour MP for Newcastle Central and West, blamed the area’s problems on Conservative rule.



She said: “The Sutton Trust figures highlight the real challenges some families in Newcastle Central and West still face.

“I grew up in a Newcastle council house, in a single parent family on benefits and thanks to the opportunities I had, I became an engineer and an MP.

“But years of Tory austerity and neglect have reduced those opportunities and when over 40 per cent of children in Newcastle are growing up in poverty, it affects their life chances.

“When there is not the money for essential services like street cleaning, when drastic police cuts are implemented, communities don’t feel valued.

“The Labour Government is working to restore the kind of social mobility available I enjoyed in many ways.



“It has scrapped the two-child limit, providing 30-hours’ free childcare, as well as free school meals and breakfast clubs for children across the country, as part of the Child Poverty Action Plan.

“It is putting more police officers on our streets and building affordable homes, and giving renters more rights, as a secure home is so important.

“Young people in Newcastle have enormous talent and potential, the same as those in London. Our job is to make sure they have the opportunities to match.”

Cllr Christine Morrissey, Cabinet Member for Children and Families, Newcastle City Council said: “The new administration are aware of the low ranking of areas of Newcastle. We have been raising the issue for some time, and we have already allocated additional funding to youth services to move forward with addressing these issues.

“Whilst it is disappointing that Newcastle has been ranked among the lowest areas in the country for young people’s opportunities, this must be viewed in the context of more than a decade of reduced public funding and increasing pressure on local services.



“Local authorities must directly benefit from more financial control and more resources through direct devolution to them.

“We make hard choices every day in the face of deprivation and we must be given the resources and the decision-making powers needed to match our responsibilities. We know what our young people need and we are best placed to deliver this. Lasting change requires sustained, long-term investment and we won’t stop fighting for it for our families.

“Local authorities are on the frontline of tackling poverty and inequality.

“We see first-hand the challenges that many families face, but we also see the difference that targeted investment and early intervention can make.

“In Newcastle we have already started implementing change to support babies, children, and young people. We have plans in place to tackle this, but local authorities need more funding to make a real difference.”



A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: “We remain committed to ensuring Newcastle – and the wider Force area – remains a safe place for people to live and work in, as well as to visit.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We work year-round with our partners to tackle anti-social behaviour and our figures show anti-social behaviour has reduced by 10 per cent in Newcastle over the last 12 months. Anyone with concerns is encouraged to report them at the earliest opportunity through our social media channels, live chat or report forms on our website.

“Those unable to make contact in these ways can call 101. In an emergency, or where a crime is taking place, always dial 999.”

News.title: Burnham vows to be ‘relentless’ on small boats after 2k migrants cross
News.content:
ANDY Burnham pledged to crack down on Channel people-smuggling gangs with hundreds more crime-fighting officers.

Labour says the National Crime Agency now has a record 791 officers targeting organised immigration crime, more than double the number at the start of 2025.



But it comes after a record 752 migrants crossed the Channel in a single day last week, the highest daily total of 2026, prompting huge pressure on Andy Burnham to get a grip on the crisis.

The Prime Minister visited Dover’s high-tech command centre on Sunday, where officials used high-tech drones to track boats across the Channel.



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood also visited the NCA’s headquarters in Stratford as ministers ramped up their border crackdown.

Ms Mahmood said the state had seized more than a thousand boats and engines, arrested thousands of criminals, and stopped tens of thousands of attempted crossings.

She said: “There is more to be done, but this Government is restoring control at our border.”

Home Office numbers show 326 migrants arrived on Saturday in four boats, bringing the number up to 2,057 since he took over from Sir Keir Starmer on July 20.

Burnham said he believed the Home Secretary’s plans were beginning to work as numbers compared to last year were down.

He said: “Although this is the peak period of the year for crossings, overall the number of crossings is down, the number of removals of people is up.



“So, there is progress, but we both recognise that we need to do more.”

But shadow home secretary Chris Philp said if Mr Burnham was serious about controlling Britain’s borders he would follow the Tories and leave the ECHR.

He said: “Labour has not smashed the gangs as they promised over two years ago.

“I saw for myself just last week hundreds of illegal immigrants departing a French beach while the gendarmes Shabana Mahmood is paying for stood by and did nothing.

“The Conservative plan is to leave the ECHR so all illegal immigrants can be deported with a week of arrival. If Andy Burnham was serious he would do this – but he’s too weak.”



Wednesday marked the busiest day for small boat crossings across the English Channel so far this year, with 752 migrants arriving in the UK.

The Home Office said small boat crossings are heavily influenced by weather conditions, with numbers typically surging during the warmer summer months.

Meanwhile Europe is on the edge after more than 60,000 migrants stormed a Spanish enclave – sparking calls to suspend free movement from the country.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Shops have been looted, cars set on fire and the streets have been turned into an open toilet in “apocalyptic” scenes.

On top of the estimated 60,000 to have entered Ceuta, another 400 crossed into Melilla, another enclave around 200 miles away.

News.title: Heroic moment citizen opens fire on In-N-Out gunman during ‘shooting rampage’ that killed three and left 7 injured
News.content:
THIS is the heart-stopping moment a heroic civilian with a handgun attempted to stop the In-N-Out shooting that left at least three dead and seven wounded.

A gunman launched a sudden and seemingly random attack at the burger restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday afternoon around 2.30pm local time, shooting multiple people and killing an employee and a customer before turning the gun on himself.



It is unclear if the death toll of three includes the gunman or not.

Hundreds of people were in the area at the time, Twin Falls police chief Matthew Hicks said at a press conference, as he described the scene as “exceptionally chaotic.”



The identities of those who died, including the gunman, have not yet been confirmed and the conditions of those injured are also unknown.

But a video taken by a witness at a nearby stoplight shows an armed civilian aiming his gun at the shooter and firing shots before ducking behind plants and the In-N-Out sign.

read more on news DARK DETAILS Lindsay Clancy breaks down as ER doc recalls desperate attempts to revive kids

Lane Koehn, who was on his way homefrom work at the time, told KTVB News that the gunman was on a “shooting rampage” and that bullets were flying all around as he appeared to shoot aimlessly and at random.

At one point, the gunman, who Koehn described as “young, pale, with glasses and black hair,” appeared to be targeting traffic at the drive-thru and nearby intersection.



He said the shooter was 30 to 40ft away from him and appeared to be armed with a semi automatic weapon when the heroic civilian opened fire, distracting the gunman.

Koehn said the hero citizen was shooting from a distance but believes it was potentially life- saving by distracting the attacker who stopped firing at traffic.

“He was exchanging fire with this other person with his hand gun,” Koehn told the outlet.



“They were both running around trying to dodge bullets it looked like, and so I went around, there’s people running all over the place, freaking out, and I park and run over to the restaurant.”

He described seeing at least one gunshot victim being helped by a worker from the diner.

Meanwhile, the shooter continued to fire off random shots “I couldn’t tell rhyme or reason..it looked like he was shooting at random…we’re not talking five shots, it’s a couple magazines,” he said.

While the exact number of fatalities is yet to be confirmed, Idaho Falls city spokesperson Josh Palmer said at least three people died and seven were injured.

Police responding to the scene found the body of the suspected gunman in an area near the restaurant.



His ID and motive is still being investigated but there is no further threat to the community, police said.

In-N-Out President Lynsi Snyder said her “heart is broken” and confirmed that an employee and customers were killed in the rampage at the restaurant that opened just a week ago on July 24.

“We lost one of our beautiful Associates tonight,” she wrote in a statement on social media.

“She was taking care of our most important asset — our Customers, and her life was taken by a disgusting human who doesn’t value the lives of others or his own.

“My heart is broken, my chest is heavy, my eyes burn from the tears I’ve shed.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives are assisting with the investigation.

Anyone with any information about the shooting is urged to come forward.

News.title: My ex pulled out my eyelashes & raped me… I made harrowing hidden recording of him bragging he was ‘proud’ of abuse
News.content:
PINNED against the door of a nightclub, there was little Suzie Mahe could do as her ex pummelled her until she was black and blue and tore out her eyelashes, spitting insults at her throughout.

After suffering months of relentless sexual and physical violence, the mum-of-one decided it was time to take a stand against Gavin Roberts, her vile abuser whose campaign of terror knew no bounds.



Afraid that Roberts would deny his wicked behaviour, Suzie took to secretly recording him, from his acidic verbal abuse to frenzied attacks which left her unable to breathe.

In disturbing footage obtained by The Sun, the vile thug can be heard bursting into a rage and smashing something as Suzie tells him to get out of her home.



As a result, the monster was arrested and eventually jailed for 15 years for 11 different offences, including one count of rape, two of sexual penetration without consent, and three counts of grave and criminal assault.

Suzie, now 31, met Roberts online in July 2022 and the relationship quickly spiralled into violence and abuse.



Roberts, 47, first attacked her at a nightclub just a few months in, leaving her traumatised, the Royal Court of Jersey heard.

“It left physical marks on my neck,” she said, adding that it felt as though the attack “lasted forever”.



The violent outburst prompted Suzie to start recording his behaviour, gradually building a case against him that would put him behind bars.

A few days later, while away on a trip together, Roberts subjected her to a horrific ordeal at a hotel, abusing her with sex toys and ultimately raping her.

The ghastly assault left her black and blue all over, with a bruise in the middle of her nose, on her eyes, chin, arms and legs.

“It was a long-winded attack that went through the night of physical punching, once again strangling and then leading to rape and using toys on me without my permission,” said Suzie.

“I felt like my body went into a protective way, and it blacked out a lot of things for me, but I still remember him stripping me naked.



“When you’re so far away from home, you’re quite vulnerable.

“You have to just let it happen to you and then deal with it afterwards.

“I was in shock that it happened to me – there was a bit of denial.”



She added that she was slowly coming to terms with the fact that he was an exceptionally violent and dangerous individual.

When Suzie confronted Roberts later in the day about the assault, he insisted she had inflicted the bruises on herself when tumbling in the lift and the bedroom.

He messaged one of her friends saying that she had gone missing and was “off her face” in a cowardly bid to cover his tracks.
