The violent episode left Suzie with lasting health issues, including vocal cord dysfunction, due to repeated strangulation, and asthma – a condition she had never suffered from before.



She was forced to undergo extensive speech surgery following the ordeal to regain her voice.

On the couple’s return from the trip, Suzie feared for her life and recorded his erratic behaviour on her phone as proof.

In one of the recordings, we hear Roberts chillingly making his way up the stairs as he loses his temper and tells her to “f*** off” and calls her a c***.

Shortly afterwards, Roberts pounced on her in yet another vile attack, strangling her so hard she vomited.

Suzie recalls how he would sickeningly gloat in his abuse, and was “almost proud” of the injuries he’d inflicted on her.



“He would look around my body at my injuries and almost enjoy it,” she said.

The monster was arrested following the assault and jailed for 15 years for 11 different offences, including one count of rape, two of sexual penetration without consent, and three counts of grave and criminal assault.

Suzie said: “Just hours before he got arrested, he once again looked at what he had done to me, and he said, ‘Do you think I could’ve killed you?’ and I said yes.”

A second woman came forward to report two separate assaults between February and September 2022.

He also received three charges of voyeurism after filming a third woman while they were having sex.



Suzie campaigned tirelessly for changes in the law to prevent others from suffering the same ordeal, including the introduction of a standalone offence of non-fatal strangulation.

Voted in on March 11 this year, the offence carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and an unlimited fine.

She said: “Strangulation is far more serious than people often realise.

“In my view, it is a clear indicator of a risk to life. I was devastated when it was treated simply as a grave and criminal assault.

“I felt it deserved recognition as a standalone offence.”



Other amendments included emergency domestic abuse protection orders, which will mean police are able to make 72-hour orders to ban alleged abusers from contacting their victim.

Reflecting on the changes, Suzie said that her campaigning has been a rewarding outcome to what was otherwise a deeply traumatic experience.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Helping secure that change has honestly meant more to me than his sentence,” said Suzie, who waived her anonymity in the campaign process.

“It means future victims will be better protected.”

News.title: Afghanistan national, 26, arrested over death of Brit woman in Athens after ‘confessing to dumping body in suitcase’
News.content:
SUITCASE ARREST Afghanistan national, 26, arrested over death of Brit woman in Athens after ‘confessing to dumping body in suitcase’

AN Afghan national has been arrested in Athens over the death of a British woman whose body was found in a suitcase.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found stuffed inside the travel bag in an abandoned building last week.



Greek police said a 26-year-old man from Afghanistan is in custody on charges of manslaughter, robbery and violating weapons law – though the exact details have yet to be finalised.

Cops arrested the man on Thursday and hauled him to police headquarters where they say he “confessed to his actions”.



He reportedly admitted his part in dumping Elisabeth inside a suitcase before hauling it to an abandoned site in Kypseli where she was later found.

Investigations by the Greek police alongside the National Crime Agency, Police Scotland and authorities in the United States identified the man has a prime suspect.



Cops analysed CCTV footage showing the Afghan national carrying a large travel bag to the site.

Cops said they believe the suspect also used the victim’s bank cards to withdraw money in Athens.

Elisabeth’s cause of death is still yet to be confirmed.

Raids of the suspect’s home uncovered a fake pistol and a knife, according to local media.



Police revealed that whoever stuffed her in the suitcase had been “careful”.

“There were no fingerprints or traces of DNA on the suitcase”, they added.

Greek cops had previously probed whether Elizabeth – a “good Samaritan” and committed Christian – was murdered by someone she was trying to help.



She was a regular traveller to Greece and volunteered for One Heart – a charity which provides medical help for refugees from Afghanistan and Iran.

She had reportedly been spotted befriending homeless people across Athens.

Critical autopsy tests were fast-tracked to help solve the grim mystery.

Police believe she was killed near to where her body was found in the derelict building.

Elisabeth, known as Lisa, was reportedly seen chatting to homeless people close to an abandoned car park where they take drugs, drink and sleep rough.



Greece’s version of the FBI are said to be “seriously contemplating” suffocation as the cause of death of the Scottish woman.

Elisabeth’s body was identified on Wednesday – the day her mobile phone was mysteriously deactivated by suspects believed ” to have intimate knowledge ” of her last movements.

A homeless man who made the grim discovery has insisted the suitcase was not in the building the two days prior.

His testimony has led police to believe her body was taken to the building at 7 Evelpidon Street on the evening of July 17 or the following morning.



Elisabeth arrived in the Greek capital on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

A Greek couple who Elisabeth was staying with in Keratsini told cops she was going to stay with some Americans she knew in Kypseli.

Investigators are now hunting the mystery pals as authorities expand the probe abroad.

“We see these Americans as key,” a source told The Sun. “We believe they have valuable information.”



It comes after reports that the friends may not be real and that Elisabeth just wanted to be alone.

So far, cops have not been able to confirm the exact date of Elisabeth’s death or if it is considered murder.

Her heartbroken father revealed he had received haunting text messages from his daughter’s phone after her death.

The dad, a lawyer in Edinburgh, told Greek cops he was sent several messages for two weeks after Elisabeth’s passing from a man now being viewed as the prime suspect.



One message sent on the last day she was seen alive said she “needed some time to herself” and “wanted to be alone for a while”.

An officer told the Sun that the emergence of the messages has helped investigators track the location of phone.

They added: ” It is clear whoever sent them was trying to buy time.”

Elisabeth’s phone was only turned off on Wednesday morning after reports of the body being found made global headlines, local media claim.



Cops are desperate to uncover what happened to Elisabeth during the three days she is unaccounted for – with the homeless man’s testimony giving them a strong lead.

The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said earlier: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time.

“We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece.

“Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland.”

News.title: Heartbreaking 1st responder testimony about desperate attempts to revive kids that left Lindsay Clancy shaking in court
News.content:
‘KILLER’ mom Lindsay Clancy broke down in court as the jury heard heartbreaking testimony from first responders about the desperate attempts to revive her children.

The 35-year-old former nurse was left shaking with her head in her hands as evidence was given on Friday, the fifth day of her trial, as she stands accused of murdering her three children.



On January 24, 2023, her husband Patrick came home from running errands to find Clancy lying injured outside under their bedroom window, and their three children dead inside their Massachusetts home.

If you or someone you know needs help or support for their mental health, text “STRENGTH” to the Crisis Text Line at 741-741 to be connected with a certified crisis counselor.





Five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson and eight-month-old Callan had been strangled with exercise bands by their mother, who was allegedly suffering from undiagnosed postpartum psychosis.

After a voice allegedly told her to kill the children, Clancy cut her wrists and neck and leapt out of the bedroom window in an apparent botched suicide attempt that left her paralyzed from the waist down.

read more on Clancy trial BLURRED LINES Hidden tactics as Lindsay Clancy's trial divides USA - murderer or victim?

Sitting in her wheelchair alongside her defense attorney Kevin Reddington on Friday, Clancy broke down sobbing and shaking as emergency medicine doctors recalled desperate attempts to revive her children.

Paramedic Jennifer Stratton told the court how she “scooped him up in my arms and carried him outside to the truck” while pictures from the basement showed an exercise band next to Callan’s Mickey Mouse pajamas which were taken off by paramedics.



Emergency medicine doctor Benjamin Kaufman spoke about trying to revive eight-month-old Callan at Bell Israel Deconess Hospital in Plymouth where he regained a pulse but had no evidence of “brain function.”

“The first thing we do is give a dose of epinephrine, and in this case, you can look directly at the heart with an ultrasound,” he explained, with hopes that the adrenaline would re-start the heart.

“His heart started beating after we were able to give that dose. At that point, we continued compressions, continued giving him breaths through the breathing tube.

“At no point in time during his care did he have any brain function.”

Callan was flown to Boston Children’s Hospital but at no point was able to breathe on his own and was pronounced dead three days later after being put on life support.



Meanwhile Kaufman’s colleague and fellow ER doctor Mark Tenerowicz, told the court how medical staff spent 40 minutes desperately trying to revive three-year-old Dawson after taking over from paramedics at hospital.

“It did not look like his heart would ever start again,” the doctor said, detailing how they gave the child IV fluids, doses of adrenaline, and other treatments all while performing CPR.

At no point did he have a pulse or start breathing on his own.

Both Cora and Dawson were declared dead at that night.

Their mother clutched tissues in court as photographs were displayed on a large screen in front of her showing the scene where responders attempted to revive her children.



They included several pieces of medical equipment including a heart monitor, children’s pajamas, and blood on the floor.



Other emotional scenes played out in court when Clancy heard Patrick’s heart-wrenching 911 call in which the devastated father can be heard screaming in pure agony, court reporters revealed.

Clancy sobbed the entire time the audio was played in court with Reddington holding her hand and a recess was called after jurors were left in tears.

Meanwhile, Duxbury police officer Stephen Hall appeared visibly shaken as he took the stand and recalled arriving at the scene and finding Patrick in the backyard while Clancy was drifting in and out of consciousness “in pain.”

While recalling working the scene, Hall took deep breathes and at one point removed his glasses to wipe his eyes.

“I heard a loud scream from inside the house,” he said, after Patrick went inside the house to check on the children.



Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial Lindsay Clancy is accused of strangling her three children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan, with exercise bands inside their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home on January 24, 2023. The former labor and delivery nurse does not deny killing them, but has pleaded not guilty and claims she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argue Clancy deliberately sent her then-husband Patrick out to collect medicine and dinner so she could be left alone with the children. The trial began with Patrick on the witness stand, describing Clancy’s declining mental health before recounting how he returned home, found her injured outside and discovered the children in the basement. Jurors have since heard his harrowing 911 call, seen the bands that were removed from the children’s necks and viewed their pajamas and other evidence from the home. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial is expected to last between six and eight weeks, meaning testimony could continue well into September.

Proceedings are scheduled to begin at around 9am ET on sitting days and normally continue through the afternoon, with morning, lunch and afternoon breaks.

Prosecutors will present their case first, calling first responders, police officers, investigators, medical professionals and other witnesses connected to the killings.

The state listed more than 180 potential witnesses, although prosecutors are not expected to call everyone named.

Jurors are also expected to visit the Clancy family’s former Duxbury home with the judge and lawyers to see the scene for themselves.

Once prosecutors rest, Clancy’s defense will begin calling its own witnesses, including people who knew her and experts expected to testify about her medication, mental health and alleged postpartum psychosis.

The defense listed more than 60 possible witnesses, but some overlap with the prosecution’s list and may not be called twice.

After both sides finish presenting evidence, lawyers will deliver closing arguments before the judge instructs jurors on the law.

The jury will then decide whether Clancy is guilty of murder or was not criminally responsible because of her mental state when she killed her children.

He added the scream had no words, “It was just a sound” and that he walked to the basement to find one of the children lying on his back, shirtless in a diaper, before all the kids were rushed out of the home by medical responders.

Hall described Cora and Callan as being “motionless” on the floor while being worked on by paramedics and detailed how he had to keep helping Clancy put her oxygen mask back on as she kept removing it.

The outcome of the murder case will largely hinge on testimonies from first responders about her physical condition and the attempt to end her life, which included critical ‘code blue’ evidence.

The jury of 12 women and six men who were taken on a harrowing tour of the crime scene and other locations related to the case on Friday, will have to determine if Clancy killed her children with intent or if she was mentally incapable of knowing what she was doing.



Her defense team argue she is not-guilty by reason of insanity, due to her extreme mental health struggles at the time rendering her not criminally responsible for the deaths of her children.

Her now ex-husband Patrick filed a wrongful death lawsuit in January 2026 against Clancy’s healthcare providers after she was prescribed 13 different medications and hospitalized several times but discharged weeks before the killings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Clancy faces life in prison without parole if found guilty of three counts of murder.

You can catch up on the trial with a recap on our YouTube Channel. Also, see our exclusive breakdown of the hidden trial tactics LindsayClancyy’s team are using to clear her.

News.title: Horror moment two firefighting helicopters collide mid-air while battling Greek wildfires as one sent crashing to ground
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment two helicopters collide mid-air while battling the wildfires raging across Greece.

One of the firefighting aircraft was seen plunging to the ground with a frantic search and rescue operation underway to recover the downed pilots and crew.



The helicopters collided near Psatha, west of Athens, after taking off from the Elefsina military airport.

Two people were onboard each helicopter.



Dramatic footage shows the two choppers drifting terrifyingly close before smashing into each other.

One of the helicopters erupts into a ball of flames with debris exploding into the air.



The helicopter plummets to the ground followed by a thick stream of smoke.

The second aircraft flies away from the crash site but appears to sustain heavy damage.

All four crew members survived the crash but two are unconscious and two are slightly injured, government officials said.

The pilots are Romanian nationals and the coordinator-liaisons – who send messages back to on-ground teams – are Greek.

The helicopters were part of an operation to tackle a huge wildfire which has destroyed over 100 homes northwest of Athens.



Greece‘s prime minister had warned firefighting aircraft could not “operate safely” in strong winds only hours before the crash.

Initial investigations suggest that the radio on one of the helicopters was not working properly, reported Greek paper In.Gr.

Aviation expert Kostas Lakafosis claimed the collision may have been caused by the pilot in the higher aircraft missing the other helicopter as it flew into his “blind spot” beneath the belly of the craft.



But ex-Lieutenant General of the Fire Department Andrianos Gourbatsis argued that a mistake had been made on the ground.

He alleged that Fire Department officers had wrongly co-ordinated the flights from the ground rather than the crew members.

Dozens of roaring blazes are being fuelled by gale-force winds across several Greek islands, destroying vegetation and burning houses.

On Saturday morning, 29 planes and helicopters began crucial water drops in Viotia, in southern central Greece, where a fire broke out on Friday.

Another fresh blaze forced evacuations on the popular tourist island of Kefalonia on Sunday.



Nearly 500 Greek firefighters have been deployed to the region, assisted by personnel from France and Romania.

Ground forces, including 18 firefighting units and 92 fire engines, reinforced 325 firefighters as they battled ferocious infernos overnight.

And firefighters continue to battle a large wildfire on the Greek island of Crete that ignited earlier this week.

Around 8,000 people were ordered to move to safety as flames closed in on southern resort villages, destroying homes, farms, and livestock in their path.

At least three emergency responders have lost their lives during the crisis, including two firefighters who became trapped in their vehicle near the mountain village of Krya Vrysi.



Fires have also broken out on the islands of Paros, Andros and Kalymnos.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes amid a spate of deadly wildfires wreaking havoc across Europe – including the UK – as the continent tackles record-breaking heatwaves.

Flames in Spain and France are understood to be dying down, leaving Greece and Turkey to bear the brunt of the soaring temperatures.

News.title: Andy Burnham backs Mirror water safety campaign as drownings spike in hot weather
News.content:
Andy Burnham backs Mirror water safety campaign as drownings spike in hot weather

EXCLUSIVE: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it was vital for people to understand the dangers of open water swimming and credited our 'Save Lives for Sam' campaign for raising awareness

The Prime Minister backs the Mirror's water safety campaign

Andy Burnham has thrown his weight behind the Mirror's water safety campaign after dozens of people lost their lives in a horrifying spate of drownings.

‌



The Prime Minister said it was vital that people understood the dangers of open water swimming and credited our 'Save Lives for Sam' campaign for raising awareness.

‌



Some 40 people have lost their lives after getting into difficulty in open water across the UK since May 24, with successive heatwaves driving people to seek respite from scorching temperatures.

‌



Mr Burnham joined the backers of the Mirror's campaign, named in memory of Sam Haycock, a 16-year-old boy who drowned in a reservoir in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, in 2021.

These are the faces of dozens of tragic Brits who lost their lives in open water READ MORE :

Water safety: Your complete guide to staying safe in the water on World Drowning Prevention Day READ MORE :

View 3 Images PM Andy Burnham has backed the Mirror's campaign for better water safety after dozens of people lost their lives in open water (Image: JASON ALDEN/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

The Prime Minister told us: "I do back your campaign, and I give great credit to The Mirror, so often a campaigning newspaper, but rightly so on this issue... It's really important that people understand the dangers of open water swimming, particularly if people are not regular swimmers, it can cause real issues.

‌



"Water safety measures around is part of it. It's also about making sure, as part of the curriculum, kids get the right swimming support, and that's I think a key part of the campaign.

"I really support what the Mirror are doing. I remember from my time as [Greater Manchester] Mayor when those incidents happen, they're so tragic."

He went on: "It's enticing sometimes to think of jumping in, but it's the coldness and the shock of that that makes people lose their breath and then struggle, and it can happen so quickly.

‌



"Credit to The Mirror; it's a really important campaign, and I would just ask everybody to listen to what you're calling for, make these changes, but also take great care. Enjoy the summer, but take great care."

The Mirror has joined forces with bereaved families and lifesaving charities to call for drowning to be treated as a national emergency. Olympic legends Becky Adlington and Tom Dean, and elite swimmer and TV presenter Michael Gunning have also given it their backing.

Our campaign calls for 'Sam's Law' to make it a legal requirement for safety equipment to be installed around high risk large bodies of water.

‌



Other demands include an urgent public awareness campaign, action to make it an aggravated criminal offence to damage or steal safety equipment, and pressure on water companies and those in control of high risk bodies of water to provide proper safety equipment. A Minister for Water Safety must also be appointed in England, as in Wales and Scotland.

Sam's dad, Simon Haycock said: "I'm over the moon that Andy Burnham has decided to back our campaign. Hopefully this will progress it and see it over the line.

"It's been relentless this summer, it just keeps coming and coming. It's really heart breaking. We need to keep the momentum going now."

‌



3 View 3 Images Sam Haycock, 16, died after jumping into a reservoir in 2021 (Image: Haycock family) 3 View 3 Images Joe Abbess, 17, drowned after getting caught in a rip current in 2023 (Image: Vanessa Abbess)

Vanessa Abbess, who has been campaigning in memory of her 17-year-old son Joe who drowned in a rip current in Bournemouth in 2023, said multiple drowning tragedies should be treated as a public health emergency.

‌



She said: "I am delighted to hear that Andy Burnham supports the Save Lives for Sam campaign. It is encouraging to hear that he understands the importance of water safety education.

"I hope he will act quickly to appoint a Water Safety Minister, who would lead the government's drowning prevention initiatives, with cross-sector collaboration and bereaved family support."

Save Lives for Sam - our demands Together, we are all calling for: The Government to launch an urgent public awareness campaign ahead of the summer holidays which targets parents and children on TikTok and other social media platforms. This should include lifesaving techniques and advice such as avoid diving into the water and information on cold water shock. Water companies and those in control of high risk large water bodies, to ‘do the right thing’ by bringing in the correct safety equipment. Compulsory lessons in schools (ahead of the holidays) on how to survive if you get into difficulty in the water, which should include the Water Safety Code, the RNLI ‘Float to Live’ campaign, and Phone-Float-Throw bystander advice. Put in place ‘Sam’s Law’. We urge the Government to make it law that safety equipment should be installed around high risk large bodies of water and make damaging this safety equipment an aggravated criminal offence to damage or steal this safety equipment. Currently it is already a criminal offence under theft or criminal damage but the penalties are low for these very minor offences. And finally the appointment of a Minister for Water Safety, as they have in Wales and Scotland, as drowning must be accepted as a preventable public health issue.

‌



She added: "Anyone can drown, no-one should, but I strongly believe through mass public service messaging and education, lives can be saved"

Ashley Jones, of the Royal Life Saving Society (RLSS UK), said: “RLSS UK is pleased to hear of the Prime Minister’s support for the campaign, and his recognition of water safety education and drowning prevention as important issues that need action to prevent future tragedies.

"Drowning is a preventable public health issue, and a broad systems approach is required to reduce the number of lives lost."

Article continues below

He called for schools to get proper funding to deliver swimming and water safety education in England, which has been pledged in Scotland and Wales.

He added: “We look forward to seeing action from the Government that follows up on the PM’s words. RLSS UK is keen to collaborate and together implement real change to save lives.”

News.title: Ghana Party in the Park organisers apologise after crush at entrance of family festival
News.content:
Ghana Party in the Park organisers apologise after crush at entrance of family festival

Police and ambulances were called to a London park after a Ghana Party in the Park descended into chaos - organisers have released a lengthy statement a "crowd surge"

View 3 Images A 'crowd surge' happened at the Ghana Party in the Park festival (Image: Plus 1 TV)

Organisers of a London festival where multiple people were left injured following a crush have apologised.

‌



Disturbing footage shared on social media shows guests screaming in terror and desperately trying to free themselves of the crowd surge at Ghana Party in the Park on Saturday. Some guests are seen falling to the floor and others are heard shouting in panic amid the chaotic scenes in the park in Barnet, north London.

‌



Three people were taken to hospital with others sustaining less serious injuries.. Now, the festival organisers have apologised and called the scenes "deeply upsetting".

‌



Witnesses saw injured people being carried from the grounds on stretchers by medics. One 18-year-old present described the incident as "very chaotic," adding that the festival was "very poorly organised".

View 3 Images Several people were left injured after the incident (Image: Plus 1 TV)

The official statement, posted on the event's Instagram page, said: "Yesterday was one of the most difficult days in the history of Ghana Party in the Park. First and foremost, our thoughts are with everyone who was injured, distressed or otherwise affected by the events that took place.

‌



"Seeing members of our community impacted in this way has been deeply upsetting. We sincerely apologise and our hearts go out to everyone involved. We wish those who sustained injuries a full and speedy recovery and extend our sincere support to their families, friends and loved ones."

But speculation on social media suggesting a stabbing had occured is inaccurate, both the festival and the Metropolitan Police confirmed. Nevertheless, following the crowd surge, the festival closed early on Saturday. Organisers said its thoughts are with those people injured and their families.

View 3 Images The festival took place at Copthall Playing Fields, in north London (Image: google maps)

‌



The statement added: " We are also aware of inaccurate information circulating on social media. We can confirm that there were no stabbing incidents at the festival and no fatalities occurred.

"Earlier in the day a fire involving a vendors [sic] required a temporary pause to the festival while the London Fire Brigade emergency services and our event safety teams responded. Once the incident had been addressed and the affected area declared safe normal event operations resumed.

"Later in the day a crowd surge at the festival entrance resulted in several attendees sustaining injuries. Emergency services responded immediately including the Metropolitan Police, London Ambulance Service, London Fire Brigade and the Air Ambulance. Following discussions with the emergency services and our events management company the difficult decision was taken to bring the festival to an early close in the interests of public safety.

‌



"For more than twenty years Ghana Party in the Park has celebrated Ghanaian culture, music and community, welcoming thousands of people in a safe and positive environment. This year's event was in conjunction with ShattaFest."

Following the incident, Met Police in Barnet said: "Officers are at Copthall Playing Fields where Ghana Party in the Park has been cancelled after an overcrowding issue at the entrance saw several people sustain non-life threatening injuries. Speculation about a stabbing is inaccurate. Please help us by avoiding the area."

"A total of 23 people received some form of assistance either from the emergency services or the event medical team, with nine people assessed by the London Ambulance Service.

Article continues below

"Three were taken to hospital, where their condition was confirmed as non-life-threatening. The event was ended early, and crowds left without further incident."

News.title: Child abuser had warrant for arrest 18 months before murdering girlfriend's toddler
News.content:
Child abuser had warrant for arrest 18 months before murdering girlfriend's toddler

Police failed to arrest Harrison Simpson, 22, despite a warrant being issued 18 months before he murdered and sexually assaulted two-year-old Isabelle Welsh

View 3 Images Harrison Simpson had a warrant out for his arrest when he murdered Isabelle Welsh (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire)

A child abuser had a warrant for his arrest issued 18 months before he sexually assaulted and murdered his girlfriend’s two-year-old daughter.

Isabelle Welsh suffered from weeks of abuse, including suffering 21 broken bones, before she collapsed at her home in Thornaby, Teesside, in September.

Alexandra Walker, 26, and her boyfriend Harrison Simpson, 22, were convicted of murder and child cruelty last week following a trial at Teesside Crown Court.

Simpson was also convicted of sexually assaulting Isabelle, while her mother was cleared of that charge.

View 3 Images Isabelle Welsh suffered from weeks of abuse before she died (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire)

Warped relationship of vile mum and paedophile boyfriend who murdered two-year-old Isabelle READ MORE :

Cleveland Police has admitted that officers failed to execute a warrant issued by Teesside Magistrates’ Court for Simpson’s arrest in March 2024, The Sunday Times reported.

The warrant was issued after Simpson failed to attend court for breaching a non-molestation order, an injunction designed to protect victims of domestic abuse.

It is understood that the non-molestation order was put in place after reports that Simpson had harassed and threatened a woman.

The force said in a statement: “Multiple enquiries and arrest attempts were carried out to try to locate and arrest him, but these proved unsuccessful.”

It added: “We recognise the time Simpson had an outstanding arrest warrant is far from adequate. A review of this was immediately conducted upon his arrest for murder.

“This review, along with a determination to continually improve our processes around suspect management, has led to a number of recent changes, such as ongoing improved visibility across the force around outstanding warrants, a comprehensive data system which tracks all outstanding warrants, and stringent oversight including a governance group led by a superintendent.”

Ms Justice Norton said Isabelle’s murder was the final act in a sustained campaign of violence, which the pair then attempted to cover up.

View 3 Images Alexandra Walker, 26, was also found guilty of murder (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire)

She jailed them for life with minimum terms of 28 years and six months for Simpson and 22 years for Walker, both minus time spent on remand. Prosecutor Paul Abrahams told the court: “This was a campaign of quite deliberate extreme violence.”

Ms Justice Norton said: “Any death is a tragedy. The death of a very young child at the hands of those who should have cared for, protected, and loved her – as she no doubt loved them – is particularly distressing for all involved.”

Article continues below

She said the toddler sustained an unsurvivable head injury in the 24 hours before she died in hospital.

The girl was sexually assaulted around the time the fatal blow was inflicted, the judge said.

News.title: Two helicopters smash into each other while fighting wildfires in terrifying mid-air collision
News.content:
Two helicopters smash into each other while fighting wildfires in terrifying mid-air collision

Two helicopters have crashed into each other while putting out wildfires west of Athens in Greece

View 3 Images A firefighting helicopter drops water over a wildfire in the area of Porto Germeno (file photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Two firefighting helicopters have collided in mid-air while attempting to tackle wildfires west of Athens, Greece.

‌



A major search and rescue operation was launched to locate the crews in the ⁠Porto Germeno area, Greece's fire ⁠department said with each helicopter having two people on board.

‌



Wildfires have ravaged parts of Greece in recent weeks and a blaze broke out northwest of Athens on Friday with nearly 500 firefighters tackling it with 23 aircraft.

‌



"During the aerial firefighting operation, two BELL helicopters, leased by the fire department, with a crew of two people each, crashed in the wider area of Psatha, Attica," the department said in a statement. "The helicopters had taken off from the Elefsina military airport. The search and rescue operation is under way."

View 3 Images Two helicopters have crashed while tackling wildfires in Greece

And in an update authorities have said that the crew members of one of the helicopters have been found "safe", while the location of the other helicopter had been found with an operation now ongoing to find the occupants.

‌



Photographs published in the Greek media appear to show the badly damaged wreckage of a helicopter on a road close to the scene.

More than 100 homes have been destroyed and people have been evacuated from their homes in the region near the Greek capital with the situation made worse by strong winds which have prevented firefighter aeroplanes and helicopters to fly near to the stricken areas.

Authorities ordered the evacuation of Kandili, Agia Skepi and Toutouli as smoke rose over the mountains. Crews were particularly concerned about Porto Germeno, a seaside community on the Gulf of Corinth.

‌



View 3 Images A firefighting helicopter flies as smoke rises from a wildfire in the area of Porto Germeno (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A military firing range has been among the sites affected, with the fire said to have activated unexploded ordnance.

The fire started near Agios Vasileios before sweeping toward Porto Germeno and into the forested mountains west of Athens. Firefighters evacuated 254 people by sea Friday and another 12 Saturday — often the last escape route when fire and smoke cut the few roads from coastal communities.

‌



Wildfire meteorologist Theodore Giannaros estimated the blaze had affected 15 to 19 square miles, though authorities had issued no official figure.

Flames are now spreading through western Attica, the region around Athens, threatening communities and an industrial district outside Megara as violent gusts prevented firefighting aircraft from collecting water from the sea. The danger carried grim resonance in a region where the 2018 Mati wildfire killed 104 people, Europe’s deadliest blaze this century.

Elsewhere in Greece, flames threatened homes on Kefalonia, forcing evacuations from inland communities as aircraft made water drops over the Ionian island. Firefighters battled another blaze near Nea Tenedos in Halkidiki.

Article continues below

Earlier this week, two firefighters died fighting a fire on Crete, while a third was killed in the Peloponnese. “A pristine forest, a paradise, was surrendered to the hands of the fire,” local farmer Minas Tzortzanis said Saturday. “There are no words to explain what has happened. Destruction. Total destruction.”

News.title: UK wildfires cause devastation to rare wildlife habitats that could take 25 years to recover
News.content:
UK wildfires cause devastation to rare wildlife habitats that could take 25 years to recover

Hundreds of wildfires devastated areas across the UK from Snowdownia National Park to Suffolk, after the driest July in England and Wales since records began

Video shows destruction of Suffolk wildfires

Rare wildlife habitats that have been devastated in the UK heatwave could take 25 years to recover, according to conservationists.

‌



Cooler temperatures forecast for many parts of the UK might ease the pressure on firefighters. But the brief respite came after crews responded to hundreds of grassland fires from the Snowdownia National Park to Suffolk, after the driest July in England and Wales since records began.

‌



Campaigners and Government Ministers warned that extreme weather could become the 'new normal' due to gobal warming. Stark images showed hundreds of acres of land were destroyed in Sychnant Pass in North Wales last month.

‌



View 6 Images Scorched earth shown after the wildfires in Wales (Image: Patrick O'Neill / SWNS)

Wildfire expert delivers sobering warning about impact of climate change READ MORE :

A major incident was declared after the flames on the Conwy Mountain forced the evacuation of 36 homes due to the fast-moving fire on July 12. Dramatic photos now show acres of scorched earth.

Much of the Sychnant Pass is in Snowdonia National Park where swathes of land are a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest. North Wales Fire and Rescue Service (NWFRS) said: "We continue to urge the public to stay away from affected areas as we are aware of people travelling to wildfire locations to take aerial photographs and videos.

‌



View 6 Images The scene of devastation follwing the recent wildfire which spread out over the Sychnant Pass in Wales (Image: Patrick O'Neill / SWNS)

"Mountain rescue colleagues have reported an increase in visitors to affected areas with the intention of 'wild camping.' This is not only dangerous but places an additional strain on resources and can hinder firefighting and emergency access.

‌



"Please avoid using disposable barbecues, ensure cigarettes are fully extinguished, take litter home and never leave glass bottles behind, as these can increase the risk of wildfire."

England and Wales are set for the driest July since records began. The Met Office described last month as an 'exceptional combination of extreme heat, abundant sunshine and an almost complete absence of rainfall'.

View 6 Images The habitat could take up to 25 years to recover (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

‌



Provisional statistics showed only 5.6mm of rain fell in England in July - less than half the previous record low of 13.4mm set in 1911. Wales saw only 7.9mm, almost a third of the previous record of 22.6mm also set in 1911. The conditions have left much of England and Wales in drought, with more than 24 million people under official hosepipe bans.

The worst blaze hit Dunwich Heath in Suffolk, which firefighters brought under control. National Trust's director-general Hilary McGrady described the loss of an important habitat for some of the UK's rarest species as 'devastating'. Adam Rowlands, the RSPB's area manager in Suffolk, told the BBC that the habitats devastated by the 'utterly sickening' fire could take up to 25 years to recover.

View 6 Images The wildfire in Suffolk devastated habitats important for some of the UK's rarest species (Image: Humphrey Nemar/PA Wire)

‌



"The acrid smell, it's not just smoke, you have a sense that animals have perished in the flames," he said. The 371-acre blaze on the heath, three miles from the Sizewell B nuclear power plant, began at the nearby RSPB Minsmere wetland reserve at 5.30 p.m. on Wednesday.

A shortage of certain food products may also hit UK supplies if the current drought conditions continue. National Farmers' Union (NFU) President Tom Bradshaw said wheat and oat yields were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they couldn't grow grass.

‌



View 6 Images An aerial view shows smoke rising from wildfires near Dunwich Heath (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Mr Bradshaw said high temperatures and drought conditions have placed all areas of farming under increasing pressure. He said vegetable producers are running low on water, which reduces the amount of food produced in the UK and increases the cost of growing it.

‌



"We can't change what's happening at the moment, there is no water in our rivers, but we must use this to take action for the future," he told the BBC. "We have to recognise that water security is a critical part of our food security and food security is our national security."

More reservoirs are needed as water collected during winter is instead pumped out into the North Sea. "We can't change what's happening at the moment, there is no water in our rivers, but we must use this to take action for the future," he added.

View 6 Images Sychnant Pass in Wales was one of the areas worst hit by the wildfires. (Image: Patrick O'Neill / SWNS)

Article continues below

He suggested farmers should be given tax breaks to build water storage systems to prepare for the years ahead. He warned: "We have taken our food supply for granted for far too long. The climates of those other countries around the world that we currently rely on to produce our food and vegetables are changing as well. It does feel like there is going to be some shortage of food products."

Drought has been declared across large parts of England and all of Wales as successive heatwaves strained water supplies, with more than 20 million people now under hosepipe bans. Amber heat health alerts have also been issued for large parts of England, including the Midlands, the South-East and the South West, until Wednesday.

The UK Health Security Agency has issued amber heat health alerts for the East Midlands, East of England, London and the south-east up to 9am on Wednesday, August 5. Yellow alerts are also in place for the North West, Yorkshire, West Midlands and the South West for the same period.

News.title: 'Royal shake-up could prove decisive for Prince Harry's public reunion with King Charles'
News.content:
Forlorn, battered and bruised from his experiences in the courtroom, Prince Harry declared he could no longer fight anymore - for in his own words, “life is precious”.

That sentence was uttered more than a year ago, following the loss of his appeal over the levels of security he believes he and his family are entitled to while in the UK.

Since Harry and his wife Meghan quit their royal roles in 2020, the Duke of Sussex has been no stranger to the court room, nor to earning incredible amounts of money at the expense of the family he left behind.

Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action READ MORE :

View 4 Images Harry with his father at the first Invictus Games in London in 2014 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Only now, after the book promos, the interviews and the Netflix series have all but dried up, he is seeking reconciliation with his loved ones that he has largely been estranged from for the past six years.

There is of course the matter of his father’s health. To his credit, Harry did drop everything, although no one can be quite sure how full his schedule is aside from his various legal disputes, to rush to be by his father’s side following his announcement in February 2024 that he had been diagnosed with cancer.

Since that meeting, which lasted just 30 minutes, Harry’s dealings with the King have been brief and showed little signs of significantly moving toward the rapprochement he now craves.

The King has shown no signs of clearing the decks for that to happen, continuing with a packed schedule of commitments and engagements both at home and abroad. Those close to him suggest if you didn’t know his diagnosis, there would be little clue to the suffering he has endured.

‌



View 4 Images Harry in happier days with his father and older brother, Prince William (Image: Getty Images)

Weekly treatments, a hospitalisation mid-way through - described merely as “a bump in the road” - and the weight of expectation he has put on himself to secure a legacy, while not fully knowing his prognosis or how his treatment may turn out in the long run.

Those in his circle suggest that is the absolute demonstration of service and duty that has become such a debate to those that have left the camp.

Long before the announcement that they were leaving their royal roles in search of “financial freedom”, Harry and Meghan plotted a scenario where they would be the first royals to create a new way of working for The Firm.

‌



The ‘half in-half out’ model suggested was roundly shot down by the late Queen Elizabeth II leading to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex having to leave the institution with nothing other than their association with the royal family.

View 4 Images Harry has said he wants reconciliation with his family (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

For a good while, that connection served as almost the sole vehicle to earning tens of millions of pounds in the corporate world, seemingly without regard to the destruction of the relationships they had vowed to honour. There is no doubt, aside from those who fawn over their every announcement or TV appearance, their star has fallen along with their global popularity.

What better way to resurrect one’s profile than to cosy up to the royal family who enjoy favourable approval ratings and a monarchy who has garnered as much respect for his global statesman role, as he has genuine sympathy for the way he has handled this particular family fallout.

‌



Harry and Meghan’s latest meeting with the King and Queen, who attended as a watchful eye over any potential deviations from the planned pleasantries, is a key moment for the Sussexes. There is little chance the Prince and Princess of Wales will welcome them back into palace grounds, let alone the royal fold.

Now I have learned that Harry wants to capitalise on this new found relationship by planning to convince his father to be by his side for the homecoming of his Invictus Games event.

It just so happens that the one man who would have had the power to convince the monarch against the idea, the King and Queen’s principal private secretary Sir Clive Alderton, is to step down from his role next year after more than two decades of service to the royal household. This may yet prove decisive in Harry’s plan to achieve a very public reunion.

‌

News.title: Prince Harry hopes to convince King Charles to join him at UK Invictus Games
News.content:
Prince Harry is hoping for a public reunion with the King at next year's Invictus Games.

If the monarch were to accept an invitation to appear at the event in Birmingham next summer, it could pave the way for the monarch and his estranged son to appear in public together for the first time in years, signalling a major shift in relations between the pair.

It is understood that the organisers of the Invictus Games plan to invite the King to take part in either the opening or closing ceremony as well as visiting a range of sporting events to meet competitors. The prince's plan could see the monarch join him at major events during the Games - or at one of the opening or closing ceremonies during the home event.

Harry has been buoyed by his recent meeting with the King, which took place earlier this month, alongside his wife Meghan and their two children, Archie and Lilibet.

‌



Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action READ MORE :

View 5 Images Prince Harry is hoping to convince the King to appear with him in public at the 2027 Invictus Games (Image: WWD via Getty Images)

The family gathering, which the Queen also attended, took place at the monarch’s Highgrove estate in Gloucestershire, at the end of a stressful week for the duke. Harry, 41, recently visited the UK for the one year countdown celebration at the National Exhibition Centre (NEC) in Birmingham.

Harry was forced to find alternative accommodation after publicly stating he would stay at a royal residence during his week long trip, only for Buckingham Palace to deny him saying he had responded to the invitation in time.

The duke was also handed a devastating loss in his high stakes legal battle against Associated Newspapers, publishers of the Daily Mail and Mail Online, when all 97 claims made by Harry and his six other co-claimants were dismissed in full.

‌



Harry, who has lived permanently in California since he and Meghan quit their royal roles in 2020, had planned for his family to join him in the UK for the entirety of his visit, but was forced to alter arrangements when he learned he would not be granted taxpayer funded security.

View 5 Images Harry is due to travel back to the UK in September for the WellChild Awards, that he has supported for 15 years (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

However, Meghan - who was due to appear with Harry on stage before she pulled out of traveling to London or attending any public engagements - and the children did eventually reunite with him later in the week, when Harry managed to secure a meeting with the King.

The duke has been buoyed by the emotional reunion with his father, alongside his wife Meghan and their children, earlier this month for the first time in four years.

‌



Sources have revealed Harry wants to arrange further meetings with the monarch to allow him to spend time with his grandchildren, who he has hardly seen since the Duke and Duchess quit their royal roles in 2020 and moved to the United States.

One insider said: “Harry’s intention is two fold. He would love the King’s support at the Games, while having his father by his side would also add considerable weight to his argument for security for his family to accompany him on the trip. “

Harry is due to return to London for the annual WellChild Awards in September, the charity he has supported for 15 years. It is understood that he will accept an offer from his father the king to stay at Buckingham Palace when he returns to Britain, marking a stunning turnaround from the last time he was in the UK.

The Mirror revealed earlier this month that Harry is to continue his controversial campaign demanding taxpayer funded security - paving the way for future visits with his family.

‌



View 5 Images Harry's relationship with the King has been strained since the prince left his royal role in 2020 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Sources close to the duke suggest his desire to have his father by his side at next year’s Invictus Games serves a dual purpose. Another source said: “Next year is a big deal for Harry. He is determined that the Birmingham Games will be the best ever and it would mean the world to him to have his father there." Another royal source suggested the King “would welcome the opportunity to see his grandchildren again”.

Harry’s case against the Daily Mail was heard in court again on Wednesday, with the trial judge asked to rule over whether the duke and other household names have to pay millions of pounds to cover the costs of their failed legal action.

A group of seven household names, which also includes Baroness Doreen Lawrence and Sir Elton John, sued Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL) over allegations of unlawful information-gathering.

‌



ANL strongly denied the claims, which were heard at an 11-week trial in London earlier this year. On July 7, Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed the claims in their entirety in a 436-page judgment and the cases returned to the High Court for a hearing on Wednesday over costs.

View 5 Images The Duchess of Sussex is keen on joining Prince Harry at next year's Invictus Games in Birmingham after cancelling plans to attend the event this year (Image: ANP/AFP via Getty Images)

The court heard there was a shortfall between their insurance cover and ANL’s costs which are more than £34 million. After the trial Harry and Baroness Lawrence, mother of murdered teenager Stephen Lawrence, called the case “an obvious whitewash”.

Harry has since returned to California and is continuing with planning for next year’s Games. He originally launched the global event in London in 2014, with the competition aiming to challenge "perceptions of disability, champion adaptive sport, and demonstrate the resilience, determination and unconquered spirit of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans”.

‌



It has since been held in Orlando, Toronto, Sydney, The Hague, Düsseldorf and Vancouver-Whistler, Canada for the inaugural winter games in 2025.

In early July, Harry travelled to Britain to attend the One Year To Go ceremony, where he competed in a variety of sports alongside former Labour minister Al Carns and TV personality Alison Hammond.

Following his visit to the UK, Harry revealed that the Games will next be held in Daejeon, South Korea. The announcement means the event, held every two years, will be brought to Asia for the very first time.

‌



The duke said he was “delighted” for the city to stage the sporting competition for its first time on the continent. The event will take place between October 6-15, 2029 in and around the Daejeon Convention Centre in Yuseong-gu. It will bring together 550 competitors from 26 nations, supported by 1,100 family members and friends in 12 sports.

Buckingham Palace did not comment.

News.title: Conman used semi-naked women to sell fake Pablo Escobar-branded flamethrowers and smartphones
News.content:
Conman used semi-naked women to sell fake Pablo Escobar-branded flamethrowers and smartphones

Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, CEO of Escobar Inc, ran an international fraud scheme where he tricked buyers of merchandise, which he falsely claimed was linked to Colombian drug lord

View 4 Images Gustafsson used scantily clad models to advertise goods (Image: Credit: Escobar Inc)

A fraudster who used Pablo Escobar’s name to market flamethrowers and luxury goods using scantily clad models which he never delivered has been jailed.

‌



Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, CEO of Escobar Inc, ran an international fraud scheme where he tricked buyers of merchandise, which he claimed was linked to the infamous late Colombian drug lord.

‌



The Swedish national, who had the nickname El Silencio, used semi-naked women to advertise the products like branded phones and an “Escobar Flamethrower” but when people bought them online, they were never delivered.

‌



He registered Escobar Inc in Puerto Rico and held successor-in-interest rights to the persona of Pablo Escobar who was the head of the Medellin Cartel and killed in 1993.

View 4 Images Gustafsson has been jailed (Image: Instagram)

Gustafsson used that notoriety to market items like the "Escobar Flamethrower" gold foldable smartphones, and a physical cryptocurrency called "Escobar Cash" at prices far lower than what would be the normal market price from 2019 to 2023.

‌



He even sent foil-wrapped Samsung Galaxy flip phones to tech reviewers to drum up public demand. When paying customers demanded refunds for non-existent goods, Gustafsson mailed them items like a "Certificate of Ownership" or promotional books instead.

View 4 Images People would buy goods advertised that never arrived (Image: Credit: Escobar Inc)

And in so doing Gustafsson raked in a $1.3million fortune but some suspicious recipients quickly noticed red flags and YouTuber Marques Brownlee highlighted the scam in a video posted in 2024. “Those people were getting scammed out of their money,” he said. “Honestly, in hindsight, I don’t know how they thought they were gonna get away with this.”

‌



Brownlee then claimed he was visited by the FBI who asked for the phone and communications which he had had with Escobar Inc.

The money that Gustafsson is alleged to have been laundered from bank accounts in the United States, Sweden, and the United Arab Emirates.

View 4 Images Pablo Escobar was the head of the Medellin Cartel (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Article continues below

He was extradited from Spain in 2023 back to the US, and he has been in federal custody since March 2025. He previously pleaded guilty in July 2025 to a myriad of fraud and money-laundering charges and has now been jailed to four years in prison by a Los Angeles court.

A statement from the US Attorney's Office read: "A Swedish national who licensed the rights of the late Colombian narco-terrorist Pablo Escobar was sentenced today to 48 months in federal prison for defrauding investors by marketing and selling products – including flamethrowers and cellphones – that he never delivered.

"Olof Kyros Gustafsson, 32, a.k.a. “El Silencio,” was sentenced by United States District Judge Fernando L. Aenlle-Rocha, who also fined him $25,000, and ordered him to pay $1,300,193 in restitution. Gustafsson has agreed to forfeit funds that were proceeds of the fraud schemes, including money currently held in a bank account in Sweden."

News.title: Burnham pledges to be 'relentless' in curbing small boat crossings
News.content:
Andy Burnham has pledged his government will be "relentless" in curbing the number of people arriving in the UK on small boats.

The prime minister said progress had been made and the government was "changing the whole approach", with enforcement officers tackling people-smuggling gangs doubled on both sides of the Channel.

"People want to see this issue addressed," he said in Dover, adding: "We also need to build a system that offers safe routes for people as well, because that also takes away the selling point of the gangs."

Political discussions around the UK's policies on illegal migration have resurfaced since tens of thousands of migrants swam into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Thursday.

Burnham noted that 98% of the people who swam to the African territory had been returned to Morocco - which he said had dealt with the immediate issue.

But he added: "There's a broader issue about the Schengen area and our relationship with it, and of course, I would want to be in regular dialogue with the EU on those issues."

His comments came shortly after the Home Office announced that the number of National Crime Agency (NCA) officers tackling smuggling gangs facilitating small boat crossings had risen to almost 800 from 376 at the start of 2025.

Burnham said there had been a similar doubling of French officers.

Asked whether he wanted to change the tone of the debate around small boats, he said that he wanted to "deal with the issue rather than play politics with the issue".

He added: "The public don't like the idea that the border looks like it's not controlled. We need to bring back that control. But also we need to offer support for people who genuinely need it."

News.title: Man admits killing Scottish woman found in suitcase, Greek police say
News.content:
Greek police say a man has admitted killing a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, days after she was reported missing.

Local officers launched an investigation with cooperation from authorities in the US, the UK and Scotland, and now say they have arrested a 26-year-old man - the BBC understands he is from Afghanistan.

The force said he was brought to police headquarters on Thursday where he "confessed to his actions". He was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, robbery and weapons offences, but the exact charges have yet to be finalised under the Greek legal system.

News.title: Prolonged drought could cause shortage of some foods, farmers' union head says
News.content:
There could be a shortage of certain food products if the current drought conditions continue, the National Farmers' Union (NFU) has warned.

NFU president Tom Bradshaw said yields of wheat and oats were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they have been unable to grow grass.

Drought has been declared across large parts of England and the whole of Wales as successive heatwaves left water supplies under strain, with more than 20 million people now under hosepipe bans.

Amber heat health alerts have also been issued for large parts of England, including the Midlands, the south-east and south-west of England, until Wednesday.

News.title: Why I don't regret choosing a vasectomy in my 20s
News.content:
Because he was asking for a vasectomy at such a young age, Sam had prepared for the questions his doctor was going to ask him: Don't you think you're too young to know you don't want kids? Could you change your mind in future? You do know reversals are expensive and aren't always successful?

"[The doctor] actually said he had very recently changed his view," says Sam. "And that, if I had come in half a year earlier, he would have turned me away instantly."

His vasectomy took place a couple of months after he first contacted the clinic.

The questions from Sam's doctor were designed to ensure he was making a decision he could live with; men under 30 are more likely to regret a vasectomy, according to guidance from NHS Scotland, external.

Dr Sarah Salkeld, a former GP who is now a medical director for MSI Reproductive Choices, a group of clinics offering various contraceptives to NHS and private patients, says a vasectomy is "very safe and effective".

But she cautions it is important for men to "really think about" whether a vasectomy is right for them.

"We offer everyone counselling to talk about it if they want to, just toâ¦ make sure they've got all the information they need to make that decision."

She says reversals are not routinely available on the NHS as there are strict criteria for having one.

The NHS website points out that other forms of contraception, external are available to men, including condoms and the fertility awareness method - avoiding sex or using condoms on the days when their female partner is most fertile.

Sam told his doctor that, while he loved kids and had a happy childhood himself, he wanted to stay focused on his job as a sound designer for video games.

News.title: Fastest runner to cross the Alps says it was an incredible experience
News.content:
Runner Sophie Woods became the fastest person to complete the 2,000km (1242-mile) Via Alpina ultramarathon beating both the men's and women's record.

Woods ran the route through storms, heat of up to 37C and dodged floods and wildfires across eight countries.

"Through the whole thing, I was only ever thinking about the day, the hour, the sort of minute that I was in", the runner told BBC Breakfast.

The previous record was 35 days and Woods did it in just 29, crediting ice cream slushies for helping her power through.

News.title: Three in hospital after fire and crush at festival in London
News.content:
Three people were taken to hospital after a fire and crush at the entrance of a festival.

Organisers of Ghana Party in the Park, also known as Shattafest UK, at Copthall Playing Fields in Barnet, London, said the event was stopped following a "major incident" at about 18:00 BST on Saturday.

The Metropolitan Police said a fire had started near the gates, which meant they were closed temporarily.

A crowd built up, and there was a surge when the gates reopened, it said.

Organisers said the decision to end the festival was made on health and safety grounds.

It said in a statement the day had been "one of the most difficult" in the event's history and called what happened "deeply upsetting".

News.title: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
News.content:
It's a Friday night. A young woman trudges back to her apartment after a day of work. She enters a spotless kitchen, unloads a bag of groceries, and unwraps a frozen pizza before sliding it in the oven.

What follows is a nightly routine that is almost meditative in its mundanity: she lights a candle and gazes briefly at the snow-covered landscape outside her window, piles a premade salad onto a plate with the pizza, and settles on her sofa to eat in front of the TV.

The tagline that accompanies the scene reads: "POV you're a childfree and single girl that has no friends and lives alone so this is how you spend your Friday night."

At the centre of the video â which has amassed seven million views on TikTok â is Lana Isa, a software sales manager in her 20s based in Toronto.

In addition to chronicling her nightly self-care routines, she takes her almost 400,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram on late-night fast food drives, reading sessions perched on a rock by the lake, even a saga of getting locked out of her apartment in the middle of the night.

Isa is part of a growing, albeit niche corner of the internet where content creators, many of them women, share their daily rituals of living alone, choosing to spotlight a lifestyle that prioritises peace and solitude - the antithesis of social media excess.

For Isa, unveiling the "no friends" aspect of her life was less of a tagline, but the "reality" she had been living for several years.

News.title: Ginger hair portraits show unexpected 'golden thread' connecting Americans
News.content:
For Kieran Dodds, photographing people with red hair has become something of an obsession over the past decade.

The 45-year-old, from Edinburgh, who is himself a "proud ginger", began taking pictures in his homeland in 2013 as part of a series examining Scottish identity.

His interest in the subject soon took him to other ginger hotspots such the Russian city of Perm and Jamaica's Treasure Beach.

His 2020 book Gingers spanned the world but after its release he noticed there was a "huge gap".

"I realised I didn't have any American citizens," Kieran told the BBC.

"Then all these people got in touch."

News.title: Body of mountaineer Nirmal Purja recovered after Pakistan avalanche
News.content:
Prince William said he was "truly saddened to hear of the tragic death" of Purja, who he said "served with distinction" as a soldier before "becoming one of the greatest mountaineers".

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme on Saturday that her organisation feared all members of the group were dead, and that Purja had led many expeditions she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit since Thursday's avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted," he wrote.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

News.title: Teenager dies after 'medical episode' at Kendal Calling festival in Cumbria
News.content:
A teenage girl died at the Kendal Calling festival in the early hours of the morning, police have said.

The 17-year-old suffered a medical episode at about 02:15 BST and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to Cumbria Police. The force asked people not to speculate about the circumstances of the incident.

It added officers were looking into the circumstances and wanted to speak to anyone who was in the area of the Calling Out tent and the Big Wheel around the time of the girl's death.

A spokesperson said: "Officers are particularly keen to speak with a group of women who alerted first responders to the girl after becoming concerned for her welfare."

They said the girl's family had been informed and were being supported by specialist officers.

The force asked people not to speculate, saying it could have a "significant impact" on the family and friends involved.

"We would ask that the investigation be allowed to take its course."

News.title: Peak District's rebrand deal brings in cash - but also criticism
News.content:
A deal between Peak District bosses and car firm Skoda to put up temporary signs welcoming tourists to "the Peaq District" in honour of the firm's new electric model has given the park authority's coffers a welcome boost.

However, it has also sparked protests from campaigners and residents unhappy about the commercial aspect of the arrangement.

One campaigner said: "If national parks are prepared to sell their very name to the highest bidder, then we're already on the path to industrial extraction of the most protected landscapes."

Park bosses have defended the "fantastic" deal and said the partnership brought in extra funds for conservation and heritage work.

With national parks continuing to grapple with funding pressures, could the partnership be a sign of things to come for the Peak District and beyond?

News.title: Ballot paper for Clacton by-election is longest in British electoral history
News.content:
The longest ballot paper in British political history is costing four times as much to print than regular ballot papers, the local council has said.

The list for the Clacton parliamentary by-election, which was prompted by the resignation of Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, is 90cm (3ft) long.

When people unfold the paper, they will find it is longer than most adults' arms.

Tendring District Council chief executive Ian Davidson - who is the acting returning officer for the by-election in the Essex constituency - said organising the vote had been "manic".

People have already started returning postal votes to town hall and most registered voters will go to polling stations on 13 August.

Davidson said: "We've logistically been looking at the size of the ballot paper, how we fold it to get it into the envelope so we can send it out to our postal voters [and] how we manage the polling stations."

News.title: Four arrested over hate crime attack on ship crew
News.content:
Three men have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a Filipino crew member of a cargo ship was attacked in what police described as a hate crime.

Two other men, both also from the Philippines, were also assaulted during the attack involving a large group of people in Avonmouth, near Bristol, on Friday evening.

Police have arrested two men aged 19 and 45, as well as a 17-year-old boy, on suspicion of attempted murder and confirmed they had received reports of racist language being used during the incident.

They remain in custody, as well as a 38-year-old woman arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

News.title: Trains in and out of London halted after trackside fire
News.content:
Trains running to and from London Liverpool Street station have been stopped following a trackside fire.

At 14:57 BST, Greater Anglia reported that a fire at Waltham Cross in Hertfordshire had halted all train movements.

The rail operator said the London Fire Brigade requested trains were stopped because of multiple fires close to the railway lines.

Services to and from Stansted Airport in Essex, Cambridge North, Meridian Water in Hertfordshire and Hertford East were all affected.

Further trains would be delayed, cancelled or diverted via Seven Sisters, a spokesperson added.

London Fire Brigade said fourteen engines were being used to tackle a grass fire near Lea Road in Waltham Abbey nearby. It is unclear whether this is a separate blaze and the BBC has asked the service how many incidents it is dealing with in the area.

Greater Anglia also said Network Rail officers were on site, "working as quickly as possible" to help restore train services to normal.

Do you have a story suggestion for Beds, Herts or Bucks? Contact us below.

News.title: Son of Wicker Man maker dies just weeks before his sequel to film premieres
News.content:
British filmmaker Justin Hardy, who directed a sequel to his late father Robin's 1973 cult horror classic The Wicker Man, has died aged 61.

His family said Hardy died on Friday night after suffering a heart attack, remembering him as "a man of family, of boundless creativity" and "so full of life right to the end".

A Bafta and Emmy nominated writer and director, Hardy was known for the documentary Children of the Wicker Man in 2024, made with his brother Dominic, which chronicled the legacy of their father's iconic film.

He had just completed production on Wrath of the Gods, the concluding chapter to the Wicker Man trilogy, which was due to premiere in London later this month.

Hardy also directed historical films and documentaries for the BBC, Channel 4 and CNN, including Princes In The Tower, Trafalgar Battle Surgeon, The Relief Of Belsen and Spanish Flu: The Forgotten Fallen.

His family said they were "devastated" by his death and "heartbroken" Hardy would not be able to see Wrath of the Gods open.

Dominic described his brother as having "an incredible appetite for life".

"We've lost him and we've lost that larger-than-life presence looking over us all," he said. "He really became a filmmaker his own right."

Dominic also praised Hardy's work on his last film as "incredibly beautiful", adding it was "a great satisfaction to him" to have made something new.

The Wicker Man, starring Edward Woodward and Christopher Lee, is the story of a police officer sent to a remote Scottish island community to investigate the disappearance of a local girl.

Wrath of the Gods was inspired by recently discovered scripts and storyboards by Hardy's late father Robin, marking the end of the trilogy that began with The Wicker Man and the 2011 follow-up The Wicker Tree.

Hardy, who also taught screenwriting at University College London, is survived by his wife Larissa, and their four children.

News.title: Gang of men hurl racist abuse at takeaway owner before violent attack
News.content:
A business owner has said that a group of men hurled racist abuse at him before punching him and smashing his head into a wall in the street in Falkirk.

Dr Zohaib Arshad said the group approached him on Grahams Road last month when he was visiting one of his takeaway shops and asked him when he was "leaving the country" before launching the unprovoked attack.

The 39-year-old, who practised as a vet in Pakistan, patched himself up with glue stitches rather than wait at A&E. He said his children are now fearful of being attacked in school.

BBC Scotland understands the police are treating the incident as a hate crime.

A spokesperson for the force said inquiries into the attack are ongoing.

Arshad stood as an Alba Party candidate for Falkirk at the 2024 General Election and is now a member of the SNP.

His political connections have resulted in the issue being brought to the attention of the Scottish Parliament, external - however he fears it would have gone unnoticed had he been any other member of the public.

News.title: Barbie sequel reportedly stalled due to eye-watering Ryan Gosling, Margot Robbie salaries
News.content:
