A sequel to Greta Gerwig’s box office sensation Barbie is reportedly in limbo due to stalled negotiations over its stars’ salaries.

Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling led the 2023 movie as Mattel’s iconic toy dolls Barbie and Ken, respectively.

The Warner Bros. production earned more than $1.4 billion at the box office and garnered eight Oscar nominations.

However, the film studio is in a race against time as the rights to Barbie will revert to Mattel if it does not make a deal with the principal talent for a sequel by December, The New York Times reports.

According to The Times, Warner Bros heads have been negotiating with Robbie, Gosling and Gerwig for months without success.

open image in gallery Talks over the ‘Barbie’ film sequel have reportedly stalled due to failed negotiations over its stars’ pay packages ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling led ‘Barbie’ as Barbie and Ken, respectively ( Warner Bros. Pictures via AP )

Two people familiar with the talks told The Times that Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav balked at offers that included a cut of the profits for the film’s stars provided it hit a box office target and a massive upfront payday of $20 million for Gosling.

A Warner Bros. spokeswoman disputed this account, saying talent representatives declined the studio’s latest offer in May and have yet to respond with a counteroffer.

“We have a rights deal with Mattel in place and have made a series of big offers to try and finalize deals to make the next Barbie film,” studio co-chairs Pam Abdy and Michael De Luca said in a statement. “Unfortunately, we have been unable to reach an agreement thus far.”

The Independent has contacted representatives for Robbie, Gosling and Warner Bros for comment.

The first film followed Robbie’s Stereotypical Barbie as she leaves the utopian Barbieland for the real world to fix an existential crisis.

It became one of just 53 movies in box office history to make over $1 billion, not accounting for inflation, and the biggest to be directed by a woman.

Robbie produced the film via her production company, LuckyChap Entertainment, which she founded in 2014 with her now-husband, Tom Ackerley. Their past productions include the 2020 films Birds of Prey and Promising Young Woman.

According to three Variety sources, Robbie earned around $50 million from the first film in salary and box office bonuses.

The film transcended the box office to become a cultural moment, fuelled by its instantly recognisable pink branding, inventive marketing and its unlikely pairing with Christopher Nolan’s Oppenheimer — a phenomenon that inspired the “Barbenheimer” nickname.

President Donald Trump’s weekend was again filled with Truth Social posts ranging from AI-generated content comparing himself to Elvis Presley and overseeing Greenland to showing off renderings of his new projects in D.C.

Between Saturday and Sunday, the president posted approximately 40 times on Truth Social, much of it consisting of AI-generated images, flattering articles and photos that stroked his ego.

“President Trump ages in reverse!” the caption of one post featuring an image of Trump read.

Some of the AI content imagined Trump as Elvis Presley, compared him to former President George Washington and, bizarrely, showed Trump capturing an extraterrestrial.

In between the strange array of posts, the president occasionally posted to condemn his opponents, lashing out at Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis for not confirming his attorney general nominee and refuting U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro’s decision to drop charges against an alleged Reflecting Pool vandal.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump shared a picture appearing to show himself assisting in the arrest of an alien ( Donald Trump / Truth Social )

In three separate posts Saturday, the president insisted that vandals had damaged the newly installed liner to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in an act of political defiance. He posted images and videos, claiming it showed evidence of such action – though it was difficult to make out in the grainy video.

His posts came after Pirro dropped felony charges against a former Olympian who was initially accused of peeling the Reflecting Pool liner – causing algae to rebloom on its surface. Pirro said evidence indicated the damage was the “result of flawed installation by the contractor.”

open image in gallery Among Trump’s flood of weekend posts was one showing him gazing at a younger version of himself under the caption ‘Same Guy. Even more energy now!’ ( Donald Trump / Truth Social )

The president also criticized Cornyn and Tillis for refusing to confirm Todd Blanche as the next attorney general, claiming they too were rebelling because of personal feelings.

Cornyn and Tillis are holding out on their votes until the Trump administration confirms it will permanently axe the nearly $1.8 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund.”

But aside from his occasional written messages, most of the president’s weekend content was a collage of videos and photos that heighten his ego.

open image in gallery An AI image shared by the president depicting him as the dynamic leader of Revolutionary War troops ( Donald Trump / Truth Social )

One AI-generated image showed Trump kissing Jesus on a cross.

Another showed Trump overlooking Greenland – alluding to the president’s desire for the U.S. to take over Greenland despite pushback from both Greenlandic and Danish officials.

In a similar vein, another image depicted Venezuela as the 51st state – seemingly referring to the president’s desire to have more control over Venezuela after capturing its leader earlier this year.

open image in gallery Trump posted an image of himself peering over Greenland ( Donald Trump / Truth Social )

open image in gallery Venezuela is portrayed as the 51st state of the U.S.A. ( Donald Trump / Truth Social )

At least five other Truth Social posts were photos of newly refurbished statues or monuments, as part of Trump’s beautification agenda in the nation’s capital. One of those included a rendering of his Triumphal Arch that he hopes to put in downtown D.C. to mark America’s 250th anniversary.

One post depicted him as a dynamic leader of Revolutionary War troops, while another showed him gazing at a younger version of himself, wearing his cadet’s uniform, under the caption “Same Guy. Even more energy now!”

In true Trump fashion, he also posted content mocking his political opponents. This past weekend’s included a side-by-side comparing Democrat James Talarico to the cartoon Alfred E. Neuman as well as a highly edited photo of Bruce Springsteen with the caption “What Happened to Bruce Springsteen?”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image that made him appear as Elvis Presley over the weekend. ( realDonaldTrump / Truth Social )

open image in gallery Trump posted a design of the triumphal arch he wants to build in Washington, D.C. ( Donald Trump / Truth Social )

It’s not uncommon for the president to rattle off a wide range of content on his preferred social media account on weekends or holidays. Trump is known for going on posting sprees on Truth Social late at night as well.

White House aides occasionally assist the president in posting on Truth Social, including Natalie Harp, who has access to Trump’s account and shares clusters of posts with his approval, the New York Times reported.

About 5,000 homes have been evacuated and about 600 homes, businesses and other buildings have been destroyed by wildfires that remained uncontained Sunday in eastern Washington state, authorities said.

The fires burned more than 8.2 square miles (about 21 square kilometers) around Spokane, the second largest city in Washington, and were among dozens across the western U.S. — stretching the ability of federal, state and local agencies to fight them. No deaths have yet been reported from the fires in the Spokane area.

While the high temperature Sunday in Spokane was forecast to remain below 80 degrees Fahrenheit (27 degrees Celsius), wind gusts from 35 mph (56 kph) to 45 mph (72 kph) were expected later in the day, said Benjamin Cossel, public information officer for the federal response team from California called in Saturday night to deal with the Spokane-area fires.

“We have weather working against us, and we have terrain working against us,” Cossel said.

There were three fires in the Spokane area, the Old Trails Fire, the Fairview Fire and the Meadowview Fire, and the state issued air quality warnings. Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson declared a state of emergency Saturday, and the National Weather Service issued a “particularly dangerous situation” red flag alert for eastern Washington.

Cossel said that as it gets warmer during the day, cool air that's now closer to the ground and keeping winds at bay will rise, allowing those winds to move through the area. The Spokane River cuts through the city of about 229,000 people, and there are steep canyons on both sides that channel the wind.

“They push the fire through the canyons, up, up the slopes, and then outside the slopes and around," he said. “It's very, very hilly, very, very steep slopes, a lot of canyons that create really turbulent, really challenging sort of wind scenarios.”

Authorities in Spokane set up a shelter at the city's main convention center.

Samantha Morton’s performance as sorceress Circe in The Odyssey has been generating a lot of awards buzz since the film’s release last month – however, the actor isn’t the blockbuster’s breakout star in the eyes of her foster mother.

Morton, 49, has revealed her foster mother’s candid review of the Christopher Nolan epic, with her former guardian preferring Anne Hathaway’s turn as Odysseus’ wife Penelope.

The Bafta-winning actor grew up in Nottinghamshirecare homes and various foster care placements throughout the 1980s. She previously shared that her birth mother suffered with mental health issues, while her birth father was an abusive alcoholic and her stepfather was jailed for attempted murder.

In a new interview with The Sunday Times, Morton revealed that she’s learnt not to be “a bighead” thanks to her childhood in foster care. “I just think Circe is a gift. But competition in art is a strange thing, isn’t it,” she said.

open image in gallery Samantha Morton with co-stars Luptia Nyong’o, Anne Hathaway and Zendaya ( AP )

“You can’t be a bighead. I’m only as good as the other good person; we are just equal and maybe that is a Nottingham thing, a working-class thing, me spending time in care.

“Art, though, depends on how we connect – I had a message from my foster mother saying, ‘You are good, but Anne Hathaway? She is amazing.’”

The actor also revealed that “trauma is a constant battle” for her, having recently lost her sister and her birth father. “I sadly lost my sister on April 22 this year. She was 53,” she said. “And I am still dealing with the coroners. And the trauma.

“I lost my real father 18 months ago. Trauma. So the past is always with me and I’m not saying I’m not going to be all right next week, but every day I wake, say a prayer and say, ‘Please help me.’”

Morton, who received Oscar nominations for her performances in 1999’s Sweet and Lowdown and 2003’s In America, revealed in 2014 that she was sexually abused by two residential care workers at a council-run children’s home when she was 13. “I wouldn't say that I live in a constant state of illness, but I do think that when you have been sexually or physically abused, it is a life sentence,” she said in an interview at the time. “It does stay with you for ever.”

open image in gallery Samantha Morton with her Bafta Award in 2024 ( EPA )

In 2024, she received the Bafta Fellowship award and dedicated it to “every child in care, or who has been in care and who didn’t survive”. Meanwhile last year, she said that the “care system isn’t fit for purpose” while accepting an OBE for services to drama and charity.

Morton is now a mother to three children of her own, including actor Esmé Creed-Miles, 26, who she shares with ex-partner Charlie Creed-Miles. She also shares Edie, 18, and Theodore, 14, with partner Harry Holm.

Morton is one of the many stars that make up the stellar cast of The Odyssey, which follows Greek king Odysseus (Matt Damon) as he spends over ten years trying to get back to Ithaca and his family after the Trojan War. The join the likes of Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Zendaya and Charlize Theron in the critically-acclaimed film.

If you are a child and you need help because something has happened to you, you can call the NSPCC free of charge on 0800 1111. You can also call the NSPCC if you are an adult and you are worried about a child, on 0808 800 5000. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adults on 0808 801 0331.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel’s rise is phenomenal but Man Utd and Carrick are doing the right thing by playing down the hype
Sports.content:
THE LOUDEST cheer during Manchester United’s pre-season friendly in Stockholm was reserved for a 15-year-old.

It was typical of Michael Carrick that he ensured JJ Gabriel’s entrance was as low-key as possible, treating him no differently from fellow arrival Jim Thwaites.



The Strawberry Arena holds 50,000 and it was roughly half-full. The atmosphere was not far removed from the soulless matches during the Covid-19 pandemic but everyone inside the bowl was clearly aware of who Gabriel is.

It was their privilege to watch him cross the white line against Atletico Madrid in the 82nd minute.



The game did not pass Gabriel by, either. He drew a foul and had a shot blocked from inside the area.

When he walked through the mixed zone afterwards, Gabriel was flanked by Luke Shaw, doubling almost as a minder.

Leny Yoro said of Gabriel: “He’s a really good player. Still really young, still a lot to learn, a lot to improve.

“But yeah, he’s really humble, still working. So I’m happy for him to get his first minutes, so I hope for him it’s going to continue like that.”

Yoro was a teen prodigy at Lille, debuting at the age of 16. He admitted: “I can see myself, because I stay humble, just want to work.

“And this is what we need in the team, even for the young guys. They’re all doing really well, and JJ is one of them.



“So I hope he’s going to learn a lot, continue like that, improve, yeah. But he’s really good, a good player.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

United’s squad against Atletico was more streamlined. Plenty of youngsters who had travelled to Helsinki and Trondheim in the previous weeks spent their Friday nights playing with the under-21s in Altrincham.

Chido Obi, once the flavour of the month, was one of them. Toby Collyer, a 22-year-old, is literally too old for the under 21s.

The writing is on the wall for those academy products. They will be sold or loaned this summer.

For United, they have to continue their sales pitch to Gabriel, his family and his advisers. He cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October 2027.



There is bound to be some resentment at academy level over the privileges Gabriel is enjoying. Those who have watched him regularly on the Carrington training pitches will argue he is worth the investment.

United are bending over backwards to ensure Gabriel commits his long-term future to them, particularly given the intense interest from Barcelona. Coincidentally, Gabriel spent a chunk of his summer in Catalonia.

He is a Nike client and they dubbed him a “future Nike icon” at the age of 14. Nike recently commissioned a painting of Gabriel, replete with their swoosh. Barcelona, of course, are sponsored by Nike.

Ruben Amorim invited Gabriel to train with the first team. Carrick did likewise before adding him to the squad against Rosenborg in United’s second pre-season friendly last month.



Gabriel’s cheerleaders have already hailed him as the youngest ever United debutant, ignoring the fact that the Atletico friendly does not count.

David Gaskell still holds that record at 16 years and 19 days old from when he came on in the 1956 Charity Shield. Gabriel turns 16 on October 6 and the League Cup fourth round is the week commencing October 26.

The third round is in September. Those dates are possibly circled in red ink on Gabriel’s calendar, if he is deemed remotely ready to debut.

His development is truly phenomenal and comparable with Max Dowman at Arsenal. Thomas Tuchel refused to rule out the possibility of including Dowman in his World Cup squad and it is a matter of time until Gabriel is on his lips.



There was a danger Gabriel could be remembered as the kid who posed for an ‘unveiling’ photo with Cristiano Ronaldo’s son. Gabriel is 11 days older than Cristiano Junior, in Al Nassr’s academy.

Downplaying Gabriel’s achievement would be wise. The calm Carrick is the ideal mentor to manage the hype and it was telling that MUTV did not ask him about Gabriel’s cameo in their post-match chat.

Thwaites, a team-mate of Gabriel’s in last season’s run to the FA Youth Cup final, was making his maiden senior appearance at the same time in Sweden. So United’s social media accounts celebrated the academy team-mates simultaneously. Low key.

United showed admirable restraint on their website. There is no separate story on Gabriel’s appearance and no mention of him in their match report. Gabriel’s father has not celebrated his appearance on his Twitter account and deleted recent posts trumpeting his son.



There are cases where the indulgence is excessive. Social media content collaborations to fuel the following and 77 is Gabriel’s squad number.

He is not old enough to learn to drive but is old enough to cultivate a growing brand.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United have a duty of care. Their academy head, Stephen Torpey, has posed for signing pictures with scholars as young as eight in a suite at Old Trafford. There are innumerable examples of too much, too young in football.

“He’s got good abilities and we try to help him to get good,” Bryan Mbeumo succinctly said. Less is more.

The ball fell kindly for the attacker, who then slotted into an open net.

The action happened so quickly after the opening goal that the cameraman barely had a chance to catch up.

ATLETICO MADRID are considering a surprise move for Manchester City outcast Jack Grealish.

SunSport understands the £100million winger has admirers at the Wanda Metropolitano due to his workrate on and off the ball.



The 30-year-old is seen as a good tactical fit for Diego Simeone, who has previously signed English players in Kieran Trippier and Conor Gallagher.

But there are some hurdles in getting a deal done considering Atletico are already well stocked in attacking positions.



Simeone has already brought in Lee Kang-In from PSG and has options such as Alex Baena, Thiago Almada and Ademola Lookman on the wing.

And Grealish would likely have to accept a rotation role if he did secure a move to the Spanish capital.

The former Aston Villa man hasn’t played since January after picking up a foot injury on loan at Everton.

He has returned to training after recovering from the issue but missed out on Man City’s pre-season tour of Hong Kong and Seoul.

Grealish has since started working with RCD Mallorca to keep himself ticking over and drum up interest from other sides.

And should a move to Atletico not work out, he could target a return to Everton after a decent loan spell saw him score twice and provide six assists.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Toffees are keen to take Grealish on another loan and see it as a realistic and risk-free move.

A return to boyhood club Aston Villa is also a possibility, five years after he left Villa Park.

Grealish played 213 times for Villa and captained the side, who are now flying under Unai Emery after winning the Europa League last season.

It’s understood Villa have discussed the idea of bringing Grealish back and believe he could offer much needed depth in the wide areas as they prepare to sell Leon Bailey to Hull.



The exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans have also meant Villa have lost some of their creativity and Grealish would provide a spark.

There are also options for Grealish in Saudi – with Al-Hilal, Al-Ahli and Neom all making enquiries.

The three clubs are prepared to make Grealish offers of between £17m and £21m a year.

And Grealish also has interest from the MLS, who believe his profile and personality would be a great commercial fit for the league.

Sports.title: Arsenal legend reveals who the Gunners’ biggest title rivals will be this season in brutal snub to both Manchester clubs
Sports.content:
PAUL MERSON has named the club he believes will be the biggest threat to Arsenal’s title defence this season – and it is not Manchester City.

The Gunners ended their 22-year wait for a Premier League crown in May, topping the table by seven points.



They are now braced to defend their title, with each of their main rivals having added to their squads.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest in a huge deal worth £116million, along with Jeremy Monga in a £10m swoop from Leicester City.



Chelsea hijacked Arsenal’s move for Morgan Rogers and paid Aston Villa £117m for the attacking midfielder.

The Blues have also added the likes of Maxence Lacroix, Danny Welbeck and Marco Palestra to their ranks.

And third-placed Manchester United have recruited Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Karl Darlow and Tynan Thompson over the last few months.

However, former Arsenal and England midfielder Merson does not believe that any of those clubs will challenge the Gunners this term.

Instead, he thinks that Liverpool will become their biggest rivals.

In his latest Sky Sports column, Merson wrote: “I don’t think Man City will win the Premier League this year anyway.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“They didn’t win it last year with the best manager in the world. They were only ever in the title race because Arsenal had a bad three weeks.

“I think Liverpool are Arsenal’s nearest challengers this season.”

So far this summer, Liverpool have welcomed new head coach Andoni Iraola from Bournemouth.

They have also signed Spanish winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna and French centre-back Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes.



The Reds are now plotting an audacious swoop for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola – who is valued at £145m by the French side.

Barcola has also been linked with a move to Arsenal, but the Gunners recently shifted their attention to Vinicius Jr as they look to strengthen their attack.

In his column, Merson highlighted concerns about City’s midfield, despite the addition of Anderson.

He believes that Anderson will not fit into the same starting line-up as Rodri.

Merson claimed: “Rodri is one of the top two holding midfielders in the world, alongside Moises Caicedo. But I don’t see how him and Elliot Anderson play together.



“Rodri is the best in the business at ticking it over, Anderson is going to be the best in the business at ticking it over. But to play both of them in there? I don’t think they need that.

“How many teams are going to have a go at Man City? People go to the Etihad and shut up shop and counter-attack.

“Do you need two holding midfielders against Hull? No, of course not. Then all of a sudden, someone’s not playing.

“Don’t get me wrong, in the big games, when they’re playing back away in the Champions League in a quarter-final or the last 16, then you need two holding midfield players. They were a bit too open in the Champions League and were well off it last year.

“But the holy grail is the 38 games in the Premier League. And there aren’t enough games in the Premier League for them both to play in the same team.

“Unless they bought Anderson and he gets a season of learning under the best in the world in Rodri. But £116m is a lot to spend on someone to be an understudy. Rodri will want to play, and he won’t want to sit there and be someone’s understudy.

“But you’re still selling one of the best players in the world.”

Sports.title: Leny Yoro insists Man United can win the Premier League THIS SEASON despite 15th-placed disaster just a year ago
Sports.content:
LENY YORO believes a Premier League title triumph is possible for Manchester United next season.

United finished third last term, having ended in an embarrassing 15th the previous campaign – their worst in 51 years.



But the appointment of Michael Carrick in January led to 12 wins from 17 games and only two defeats, fuelling hope among United fans of an end to their title drought.

Rivals Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea appointed new managers in the summer, while Roberto de Zerbi was installed at Tottenham in late March.



With champions Arsenal the team to beat, United have emerged as potential challengers amid a rare prolonged period of stability under Carrick.

Yoro echoed team-mate Bryan Mbeumo’s promise of a “big” season when asked if United can win the title.



The Frenchman said: “Yeah, of course. We’re Man United so we have to think like that. And I know we have the potential to do it, so we have to do it.

“The mood is really good. We work really hard, and outside the pitch, we have a good vibe, good mood.

“So the target this season is to win every game, to be honest. For the team to be the best, for myself to do good games every time, to win trophies, and to be at the top.”

United came from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in their third pre-season friendly in Stockholm on Saturday.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Centre back Yoro started at right back for the third game running in the absence of Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, who will report for pre-season after their post-World Cup breaks on Monday.

United signed Yoro from Lille for £58.7million in July 2024 and the 20-year-old has made 33 appearances in each of his campaigns due to a combination of injuries and competition.

Fellow centre half Matthijs de Ligt is certain to miss the start of the season after back surgery while Lisandro Martinez sustained a thigh injury in the World Cup final, though he is not expected to miss any United games.

Carrick has played Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven at centre back in a right-footed-left-footed combination in pre-season, with Yoro filling in at right back.

Yoro was keen to stress he is a centre back first and foremost but acknowledged it is time he established himself at United in his third season.



He added: “I hope I’m not going to be injured this pre-season. That will help me to improve as well, and to be ready for the start of the season.

“But the team is doing really well. No injuries yet as well. So hopefully we’re going to continue like that.

“I know I did a great season but I know I can do much, much better. I know my potential, for sure, and I hope I’m going to have a really good, good season.

“Obviously, I have no excuses, but I hope I’m not going to be injured this season, and I’ll show to everyone what I can do.



“Sometimes people forget I am still only 20, still a lot to learn, so I have a lot to improve.

“And like I said, I know my potential, I can learn a lot. I can improve a lot.

“So I hope this season’s gonna be a big, big step for me as well.”

Liverpool will hope that Andoni Iraola will be able to steady the Reds following a disastrous second season under Arne Slot but former hero Phil Thompson believes a title tilt could be on the cards

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is set to oversee his first campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool hero Phil Thompson believes the Reds could be contenders for the Premier League title under Andoni Iraola - but only if they avoid major injuries. The former Bournemouth boss was handed the reins this summer following the decision to sack Arne Slot.

‌



The Dutchman lifted the Premier League crown in his debut season at Anfield but the Merseysiders struggled to hit those heights last term. Liverpool slipped to fifth in the table, just about squeezing into the Champions League.

‌



Since then, they have lost legendary figures Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson, while Ibrahima Konate quit the club for Real Madrid. Liverpool have invested since then, sealing deals for Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, while they are chasing a big-money transfer for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola.

‌



Giving his verdict on his former side, Thompson believes that another push for the title could be on the cards should Iraola have his star players available throughout the whole season.

"Iraola will need all of his players fully fit, but if we have a fully fit squad, we have a chance of winning the league this year, without question," Thompson told the BBC. “The fans want to see a bit more aggression, but I could see, just from watching (pre-season) from the stands, the demands of the manager.

And while a lack of injuries might push Liverpool up the table, Thompson also believes that having vocal leaders in the dressing room might also be a useful asset under their new boss.

"When you have a difficult time — a difficult couple of games or something — you need some strong voices in there, and you just feel like there is only Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker who remain at the club," Thompson added.

"I know people go, 'Oh, Dominik Szoboszlai'. But he has only been there a couple of years. He has to step up and I think he will do.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Thompson has shared his thoughts on Liverpool ahead of the new season (Image: Getty Images)

"But there are others around the team who you look to who will have to step up, to lay down some player rules."

Liverpool have just three more pre-season friendlies to navigate against Leeds, Monaco and Como before they kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign. The Reds get themselves underway against Newcastle United away from home, before their first match at Anfield against Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot

A source described the FIFA President as a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor

Donald Trump addresses his call to Infantino over Balogun

Gianni Infantino looks certain to be ousted as FIFA President after his 'shabby' attempts to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



Infantino, 56, could have profited from the "Fifa Forward Enterprise" scheme (FFE) and is trying to stay in his post. But his support is flooding away.

‌



A source told the Sunday Times that Infantino is a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor.

‌



The FA and UEFA, European football's governing body, said that they had lost confidence in Infantino.

In a stinging statement, which the English FA said it supported, Uefa described the scheme as a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal he [Infantino] hatched and tried to force through".

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

View 3 Images And it's goodbye from him: Sources suggest Infantino's days at FIFA are numbered (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



It added: "The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family."

Former FA chief Mark Pallios was among those calling on Infantino to go. He said: "He should not survive.

"He has delivered these plans with a complete lack of transparency." England legend Peter Reid slammed Infantino and called for him to resign for the good of the game.

‌



He told the Mirror: "He must go - look at the World Cup: the hydration breaks for advertising, the half time show in the final.

"FIFA has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots."

CONCACAF, which governs the north and central American associations, plus the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" with Infantino's presidency.

‌



View 3 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino speaks during the 2026 World Cup draw (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident," CONCACAF said in a statement. "It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

"This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

‌



Uefa led the way in opposing the plan with its 55 members, including the FA, agreeing on Thursday to boycott all Fifa competitions.

"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game," it said.

"We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story.

‌



"The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in Fifa has only just begun."

Sources told the Sunday Times that senior figures in FIFA were looking to find a successor to Infantino.

View 3 Images Peter Reid the England legend called for Infantino to resign (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



A spokeswoman for the FA said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Infantino is likely to face an emergency FIFA council meeting where he will be asked to resign.

If he refuses, a single candidate backed by all his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year's election.

Article continues below

Candidates for the role include Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football president Sheikh Salman and Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al Khelaifi.

There may also be support for a less high-profile candidate who has backing from across the various continents.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go

Gianni Infantino has been told to leave FIFA following the doomed plan to sell off the World Cup with UEFA and CONCACAF declaring losses of confidence in the current president

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has u-turned on the plan to sell a share in the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has been told to RESIGN from FIFA by a whopping 99% of Mirror readers. The president finds himself under huge pressure, having performed a dramatic u-turn on his plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to an investment group.

‌



FIFA announced the plot earlier this week, to widespread criticism from fans, governing bodies and even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. There were suggestions that some confederations would consider boycotting any FIFA-organised competitions in the face of the plan.

‌



But Infantino and FIFA performed a huge backtrack by cancelling the proposal in its entirety. That, however, has not seen the current president escape criticism, with some still calling for the 56-year-old to be removed from his position.

‌



Since the baffling plan was originally unveiled, Mirror Football has been running a poll for fans to decide whether Infantino should resign or not. In total, 6832 fans had their say, with a huge 99 percent of them suggesting that Infantino’s position was now untenable.

That vote follows UEFA declaring a loss of confidence in the current president. A statement from UEFA on Saturday: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA.

“You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been told to leave his post (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

CONCACAF followed suit with their own scathing statement, while bizarrely the Qatari FA have spoken out in support of Infantino.

A statement read: “We welcome FIFA President Gianni Infantino's decision to withdraw the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal in the interest of the global football community.

Article continues below

“While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among Member Associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition

Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison was diagnosed with neurological condition Ramsay Hunt Syndrome earlier this year but he now appears to be firmly on the mend

View 2 Images Andy Morrison previously captained Man City (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Man City captain Andy Morrison has revealed how he has left doctors ‘amazed’ with his recovery from Ramsay Hunt Syndrome. The 55-year-old was diagnosed with the devastating neurological condition earlier this year.

‌



The condition is caused by a virus in the facial nerve and can lead to face paralysis, blistering rashes near the ear, severe earache and hearing loss. But it appears that the former City man is firmly on the mend, having issued an update to supporters on social media following a return to the commentary booth.

‌



He said: “Evening everyone. Just a quick update after the first day back working at City with the matchday live team, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

‌



“It was fantastic to be back. Felt the voice was strong enough to go back and do co-commentary today. That's my first time back in five-and-a-half months. I really appreciate all the support and working with Ali Mann, who makes it very easy.

Arsenal star refused to go on pre-season tour to force through summer transfer READ MORE :

“An enjoyable game. I struggled with a few words, a few names, but nothing too bad. I did struggle with (Ryan) McAidoo. Could have a player there by the way, watch this space. There was enough there to think he could be the next one on the conveyor belt, hugely impressive in the second-half.

‌



“Birthday yesterday, that was a great day with grandkids and family. I had a specialist on Wednesday and it was really positive, he was really delighted and amazed at the progress I had made, from House-Brackmann (nerve grading scale) six to a four and he is really positive that within a year I'll get my eye back and be able to blink, so I won't have to tape it down at night.

“I still have to take juice to swallow and I have no taste in the side of my mouth and the whole side of the face is numb, so I have to drink through a straw still. He wasn't sure just how much that would progress because it's still really weak. But if sucking through a straw is worst case scenario then so be it. I won't be posting now because I won't see a specialist for another three months.

View 2 Images Andy Morrison has offered an update on his condition (Image: @AndyMorri5on/X)

Article continues below

“A really good day and it just felt great to be back doing something when that seemed a million miles away. I didn't get out of bed for four weeks and couldn't speak for a month.

"I had some really dark days in this conservatory but I stayed positive and this too shall pass, everything passes, good or bad, everything comes and goes and sometimes you just have to dig in and get through it. But thanks for listening and see you all soon.”

Sports.title: Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear

Manchester United have already been busy in the transfer market under Michael Carrick and some exits could be on the cards before the end of the window but one deal is already under threat

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has some decisions to make in the transfer market (Image: Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee might just have seen his Manchester United exit route blocked, with Juventus pursuing alternative targets. The Dutchman was expected to leave Old Trafford this summer following a disappointing couple of seasons.

‌



Zirkzee, 25, joined the club from Bologna for a fee of £36.5m in 2024 but he has gone on to score just nine goals since then - just five of those coming in the Premier League. It was previously suggested that United were happy to cut their losses on him this summer.

‌



A return to Serie A was touted for the former Bayern Munich man, with Juventus emerging as potential suitors. But a switch to Turin now looks unlikely given Juventus’ own business.

‌



According to reports in Italy, the Old Lady are closing in on a permanent deal for French striker Randal Kolo Muani for a fee of around £42m (€50m), while they have also completed a move for Bayer Leverkusen’s Kerim Alajbegovic.

Amad and Leny Yoro in total agreement after JJ Gabriel makes Man Utd debut READ MORE :

Given those two moves, it appears unlikely that Juventus will want to sign Zirkzee as well. The only route to a move to Turin appears to be a swap deal involving the Dutch forward and Francisco Conceição, albeit it remains to be seen whether that is an avenue that the Red Devils want to explore.

He does also appear to have other interest, specifically from Ajax and Premier League sides, but whether that becomes a tangible move, is another matter. It could leave Zirkzee in a very tricky spot, with Carrick appearing to signal that the forward has little future at Old Trafford, having only given him a brief cameo in the pre-season win against Atletico Madrid.

‌



Fellow forward Bryan Mbeumo instead started centrally and enjoyed a productive evening by scoring twice. Speaking about his role, the Cameroonian said: “Obviously, I’m lucky to be able to play a different position and I try to give my best. It depends on the games (where I play).

View 2 Images Zirkzee was only handed a brief cameo vs Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

“We try to get ready for the first game of the season and we work really hard on the training so it’s really important to have good results as well.

Article continues below

He added: “Obviously I’m always really challenging myself every time and will never regret having this challenge.”

Away from Zirkzee and Mbeumo, United could potentially be left with a decision to make over Benjamin Sesko. According to reports in Germany, Bayern Munich remain interested in the former RB Leipzig man, albeit their focus for now remains on agreeing a new deal with star forward Harry Kane.

Sports.title: Dunkley leads Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds
Sports.content:
Sophia Dunkley's 56 off 33 balls fired the Trent Rockets past SunRisers Leeds in an impressive victory by five runs in The Hundred at Trent Bridge.

Opener Dunkley's imperious innings was aided by a useful contribution from her international team-mate Nat Sciver-Brunt (33 off 25) and a cameo from Bess Heath to leave the Rockets with a middling - but defendable - score of 139-7 after their 100 balls.

Australia star Ash Gardener (1-18) delivered for the home side, taking the early wicket of opener Bryony Smith (10 off 12) and limiting the top-order scoring of Jess Jonassen (19 off 18) and Phoebe Litchfield (24 off 22) to leave SunRisers Leeds well behind the required run-rate at 73-3 off 64 balls.

Image: Phoebe Litchfield managed 24 off 22 before being dismissed by Charley Phillips

Annabel Sutherland, though, reignited hope for the batting side with a brilliant 59no off 30 deliveries, but it was too little too late for the visitors as some tidy bowling by Kim Garth (0-26) at the death - despite a last-ball maximum by Sutherland - meant the Rockets held on and secured an important victory.

The win consolidates their strong position as they remain second in the table, while SunRisers Leeds, languishing in seventh, take another damaging blow to their Eliminator chances.

Wyatt-Hodge out for rest of Hundred

Image: MI London's Danni Wyatt-Hodge has been ruled out of The Hundred due to injury

England's medical team have ruled batter Danni Wyatt-Hodge out of the remainder of The Hundred.

MI London's Wyatt-Hodge sustained a left calf tear during her innings of 52 not out in a narrow defeat by Southern Brave on July 27.

"Following a scan and assessment by England's medical team, it has been confirmed that she will miss MI London's remaining matches in The Hundred," an MI London statement read.

Wyatt-Hodge has been replaced in the MI London squad by Ella Claridge and faces a race against time to be fit for England's three-match ODI series with Ireland in September.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Blue Bolt and Precise clash again in Prix Rothschild
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Sunday with Flat action from Chester, Yarmouth and Deauville, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.40 Deauville - Star fillies Blue Bolt and Precise lock horns again

A red-hot renewal of this Group One Prix Rothschild at Deauville where Blue Bolt and Precise renew their rivalry.

Andrew Balding's Blue Bolt saw off Precise when landing a first Group One success in the Falmouth at Newmarket last month and bids to confirm that form under Colin Keane. A dominant winner on that occasion, the market believes she can follow up and land a four-timer.

Balding said: "She seems in good nick and if she repeats the performance from Newmarket she will take a lot of beating.

"She's been a star this year and the only factor is she has never travelled far from home to run before. But if she takes the travel in her stride then she should hold every chance of continuing her winning run."

Aidan O'Brien saddles Precise, herself a four-time Group One scorer, with Ryan Moore in the plate. An impressive winner of the Irish 1000 Guineas, she took the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot before failing to land a blow on Blue Bolt. Sent off the odds-on favourite that day, it will be fascinating to see if she can reverse the form.

O'Brien said: "She's in good form, she was stood in the gates a little bit long the last day and lost a couple of lengths and turned her head a little bit.

"Hopefully she won't do that the next day and give away those lengths. It's hard to do that at somewhere like Newmarket, especially at the July meeting where you are going straight down. We're happy with everything she's doing and looking forward to seeing her again, she's been a special filly for us so far."

Moon Target has two lengths to find on her fourth behind Precise at the Royal meeting, while Green Spirit might appreciate the drop back to a mile.

A deep contest has several with each-way claims including Karl Burke's 1,000 Guineas runner-up Evolutionist.

3.20 Chester - Unbeaten Lifeplan heads the field

Declan Carroll's Lifeplan faces eight rivals as he bids to remain unbeaten in a cracking edition of the Listed Queensferry Stakes at Chester.

Last year's Gimcrack champion has not been seen since landing that prestigious prize back in August and his connections are hoping he can make up for lost time. Stall nine will make life a bit trickier for jockey Zak Wheatley however.

Song Of The Clyde is a top performer on his day and showed all his ability when taking the Listed Carnarvon Stakes at Newbury. Below his best the last twice, he will not want conditions to be too quick.

Hugo Palmer fields Fitzella and Ardisia who are both closely matched on the pick of their runs, while Calico Blue steps up in class for Roger Varian.

12.56 Deauville - Woot Woot, Nicely and Queen Of The Day clash

A strong edition of the Sky Sports Racing Prix Six Perfections where a host of in-form two-year-old clash over seven furlongs.

Christopher Head has never hidden his admiration for Woot Woot and she justified that reputation when winning impressively at Saint-Cloud and she warrants respect on this grade.

Queen Of The Day defeated Woot Woot on debut before chasing home the exciting Avec Toi on her second start and she will find this an easier task.

British raider Nicely stepped forward from her debut to win comfortably at Hamilton and adds further intrigue to this splendid opener.

Best of the rest

1.32 Deauville - Group Three contest with Light Of Dawn representing Wathnan Racing and Karl Burke. Jorolina and Kosuma look useful.

3.05 Deauville - Group Three where Elle Eclipse and Lefteye feature. Evita has good form behind Diamond Necklace. William Buick rides Symbol Of Majesty.

10.09 Saratoga - Grade Two Glen Falls - rescheduled with Survie and Gezora fancied.

3.52 Chester - Power Fizz and Monarch's Gold involved alongside Roman Dragon.

3.08 Yarmouth - Valuable novice.

Sports.title: Staveley-led consortium agrees deal for minority stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
Vanessa Gold has confirmed she has agreed to sell her stake in the club to a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.

Gold, who succeeded her father David as joint-chair of the Hammers following his death in 2023, has a deal in place with a group headed by Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners for her family's 25.1 per cent holding.

However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Image: Former Newcastle co-owner Staveley's consortium is set to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the club

"Amanda Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, PCP Capital Partners along with Ashland Forest Capital Partners can confirm they have agreed the purchase of the Gold family's 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United," the Staveley-led consortium said in a statement.

"A legal binding agreement has been signed.

"This sale agreement, though, remains subject to a pre-emption process under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"No further comment will be made whilst the ongoing legal process takes its course."

Sky Sports News further understands Staveley, Ghodoussi and their consortium have brought together considerable funds.

Kretinsky voices displeasure at decision

In June, the club announced that co-owner Daniel Kretinsky was set to become West Ham United's largest shareholder after agreeing a deal to buy the Gold family's stake in the club.

The statement issued in June said they hoped to finalise the transaction within a couple of weeks, but that milestone has yet to be reached.

Kretinsky was due to increase his shareholding to 43 per cent, exceeding the current 38.8 per cent owned by David Sullivan, who has since released a statement in response to the latest development, expressing his disappointment over the Gold family's decision to sell their shares. It read:

"The agreement we had reached with the Gold family in June provided stability for the club at a crucial time.

"Today's [Saturday] announcement does the opposite.

"We will always act in the best interests of West Ham United and are reviewing all of our options, including exercising our pre-emption rights in full."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of West Ham's pre-season friendly against Stevenage

Gold said in a statement: "As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint-chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023.

"Whether as a youth-team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father's priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

"On June 12, Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

Image: The consortium is led by Staveley and her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, alongside PCP Capital Partners

"Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham.

"While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club's best interests, as my father did and would expect of me."

Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club's rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on August 16.

West Ham said in a statement: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from joint-chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation. Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

"The club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."

Sports.title: Warrington go fourth as Wakefield move second, Saints beaten by York
Sports.content:
Super League: Warrington move into fourth with comprehensive win over Castleford, St Helens beaten by York in thriller, and Wakefield regain second

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Warrington Wolves wrapped up a big win over Castleford Tigers Highlights as Warrington Wolves wrapped up a big win over Castleford Tigers

Warrington Wolves moved up to fourth in the Betfred Super League table after recovering from a lacklustre start to claim a comprehensive 48-18 win at Castleford Tigers .

Having lost four of their last six matches, including three in a row on the road, Warrington were made to pay for an error-strewn first 20 minutes as the Tigers went 16-6 ahead at the OneBore Stadium.

But Matty Ashton, Toby King and Toafofoa Sipley touched down to turn the tide and put Warrington 24-18 in front at half-time, and James Harrison and Leon Hayes extended the Wolves' lead after the break.

Ashton scored again, taking his tally to five tries in two matches against Castleford this year having bagged a hat-trick when Warrington claimed a 72-6 victory in March, before Ben Currie scored.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Teenage scrum-half Ewan Irwin was excellent with the boot, splitting the posts with all eight conversions, to make it back-to-back defeats for Castleford.

While Castleford were stuffed by rivals Wakefield last weekend, they claimed a shock win over Leeds in their last home match and Warrington head coach Sam Burgess had warned they would be no pushovers.

On this occasion, they could not find the defensive intent required to stop Warrington on their push for a spot at the top end of the top six.

Sailor misses late kick as York edge thriller

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as York Knights clinched a thrilling victory over St Helens Highlights as York Knights clinched a thrilling victory over St Helens

Oli Field's double further dented St Helens' play-off hopes despite Jack Welsby's try-of-the-season contender as York edged to a thrilling 34-32 victory at the LNER Community Stadium.

Saints got off to the perfect start when Welsby kicked through to allow Jake Davies to touch down, with Jackson Hastings adding the conversion.

York Knights inflicted a damning loss on St Helens

York hit back almost immediately when Toa Mata'Afa put Jon Bennison over in the corner, and although he was unable to convert his own score, he was successful after Field capitalised on Cody Hunter's well-timed pass with a neat step to make it 10-6.

The lead proved short-lived when Hunter was unable to claim Hastings' up and under and Shane Wright pounced to score a converted try, and the visitors surged further head when Welsby burst through Denive Balmforth's tackle after the fleet-footed Harry Robertson had raced down the right wing.

However, Balmforth swiftly made amends with a sniping finish and Bennison levelled it up at 16-16 at the break.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The Knights were temporarily reduced to 12 when Ata Hingana was sent to the bin for a high tackle on Davies, but it was they who regained the lead with 53 minutes gone when prop Paul Vaughan barged his way over and Bennison added the extra points.

They went 12 points ahead after Saints failed to deal with Hunter's lofted kick, Nikau Williams touching down and Bennison making it 28-16, but Robertson's brilliance allowed Tristan Sailor to feed Welsby to complete a length-of-the-field move which was converted by Hastings.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Field's second try and a fifth successful Bennison conversion gave the Knights breathing space, but late scores from Robertson and Jacob Douglas gave Saints a chance.

Regular goal kicker Hastings remained on the field but was holding his glute so Sailor had to deputise and missed the crucial kick to level the game.

Wakefield move back second with win over Catalans

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Wakefield Trinity sealed victory over Catalans Dragons Highlights as Wakefield Trinity sealed victory over Catalans Dragons

A crucial double from Isaiah Vagana helped Wakefield Trinity to a 32-12 win over Catalans Dragons to move back into second place in the Super League table.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The match was close at the break, Trinity leading by just four points, but a five-minute spell changed the game thanks to Vagana's quick efforts.

Jake Trueman and Cameron Scott had gone over early to give the visitors the lead before Catalans responded through Toby Sexton.

After Caleb Hamline-Uele and Matthieu Laguerre then put more points on the scoreboard for both outfits, Vagana's moment arrived with just 15 minutes remaining before Scott sealed the deal with his second.

The night was dampened further for Catalans with one minute remaining when Ugo Tison was sent to the sin bin for his hit on Jack Sinfield.
