World.title: New Riga rail link boosts Elron's Baltic passenger numbers
World.content:
More than 19,000 passengers traveled on Elron's Baltic routes in the first half of 2026, as the new Tallinn-Tartu-Riga rail link fueled growing demand.

Over a third of international passengers traveled between Tartu and Riga in the first half of the year, with demand increasing after Elron launched a direct Tallinn-Tartu-Riga connection in January.

"Passenger interest in traveling by train to Latvia and Lithuania, and vice versa, has grown significantly," said Kristo Mäe, head of Elron's international business.

Mäe said the new direct route has increased demand across Elron's international network, with monthly passenger numbers rising from about 2,000 in January to nearly 4,400 in June.

"Interest has also grown in the Tallinn-Tartu-Riga-Vilnius service launched in January 2025," he added.

Last year, over 16,000 passengers bought direct tickets between Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. In the first six months of 2026 alone, meanwhile, Elron's international routes have already carried more than 19,000 passengers, Mäe noted, with another 1,700-plus using the Tallinn-Tartu-Riga direct train for travel within Latvia.

Elron currently operates the direct Tallinn-Tartu-Riga service as well as the Tallinn-Tartu-Valga-Riga-Vilnius route, which requires a transfer in Valga. An additional Tallinn-Tartu-Valga-Riga service runs on weekends.

An Elron departure to Tartu displayed at Riga Central Station. January 2026. Source: Elron

Tartu was the most popular departure point or destination for Elron's international trips, with 10,825 passengers, followed by Tallinn with 6,347.

The busiest route segment was Tartu-Riga, which accounted for 7,500 passengers, or 38 percent of all passengers on Elron's international routes.

Latvians riding locally

More than 10,000 passengers traveled to and from Valga on routes toward Latvia and Lithuania during the first half of the year, according to data from Elron and Latvian rail operator Vivi.

The direct Tallinn-Tartu-Riga service launched on January 12 accounted for 8,287 international trips during this period.

The most popular segment was Tartu-Riga, which made up 42 percent of journeys, followed by Tallinn-Riga (13 percent), Valga-Riga (9 percent), Tartu-Cesis (nearly 6 percent), Tartu-Valmiera (over 5 percent) and Tartu-Sigulda (4.5 percent).

Since March, Elron has also sold tickets for domestic Latvian journeys on the Tallinn-Tartu-Riga train.

From April through June, more than 1,700 Latvian passengers used the service within Latvia, most commonly traveling between Riga and Cesis (30 percent), Riga and Sigulda (26 percent) or Riga and Valmiera (14.8 percent).

World.title: Travel insurance may not cover canceled concerts abroad
World.content:
Canceled concert abroad? Some travelers may be stuck paying for unused hotels and transportation if their insurance policy doesn't include event cancellation coverage.

The issue recently affected fans in Estonia who had planned to travel to Riga last week for a Pitbull concert that was canceled last-minute due to technical issues, leaving some with nonrefundable travel and lodging expenses.

Latvian public broadcaster LSM reported that 40,000 tickets had been sold for Pitbull's gig at Mežaparks Great Bandstand.

Estonian Insurance Association (EKsL) chair Tuuli Pärenson said standard travel insurance often does not cover losses caused by an organizer canceling an event.

"In cases like this, the insurance policy should be more than the basic coverage, which usually doesn't cover event cancellations," Pärenson said.

She noted travelers should specifically choose additional coverage, adding that not every Estonian insurer offers it.

Depending on the insurer, that protection may be sold as an optional travel insurance add-on, as part of trip disruption coverage or included in broader travel disruption policies.

In Estonia, LHV and BTA Insurance offer optional coverage for canceled events.

Joonas Kušvid, head of personal claims at If P&C Insurance, said his company's travel insurance does not cover expenses when an event is canceled by the organizer.

"In the Pitbull case specifically, we have two customers who contacted us after booking other accommodations and other arrangements," he said. "However, because the event was canceled by the organizer, it does not qualify as an insured event under our policy."

World.title: Estonian island hosts dozens of pop-up cafes in annual summer tradition
World.content:
Over three dozen pop-up cafes opened across Hiiumaa over the weekend, bringing islanders and visitors together for the 20th edition of the beloved local summer tradition.

The tradition began in Kärdla, the island's capital, and in the two decades since has grown into one of the island's biggest summer events, with residents turning their homes and backyards into cafes for a day or two and serving up homemade treats.

Hiiumaa Home Cafe Days is especially popular among island natives who now live elsewhere but return each summer to reconnect with their roots.

"I'm one of those people who lives on the mainland but still considers themselves a Hiiumaa islander, because my roots are here," said Ester. "And every year I have to come back and get a taste of these cafe days."

After waiting in line at one of the island's pop-up cafes with other visitors, it was finally Kairi and Marietta's turn to pick out their favorites. Kairi went for a slice of savory sandwich cake with tuna.

Marietta, meanwhile, chose a piece of cookie cake after spotting a handwritten note saying it had been made by someone named Laura late the night before.

"Our mom always made homemade cookie cakes late at night before our birthdays," she recalled.

Signature summer event

Among the cafes' customers this weekend was Prime Minister Kristen Michal, who had nothing but praise for the lively atmosphere.

"This is an incredible event," Michal confirmed. "As you can see, there's a lot going on here, people are lining up and all the pop-up cafes are wonderful."

Kristel Peikel, head of the Hiiumaa Tourism Cluster, called the pop-up cafe weekend the island's signature summer event, comparing its importance to the neighboring island's Saaremaa Opera Days.

"And this year we have extra reason to celebrate: a record 39 cafes are taking part across the island for the 20th edition of Hiiumaa Home Cafe Days," Peikel said.

World.title: Center Party leader backs temporary border controls over migration concerns
World.content:
Center Party chair Mihhail Kõlvart backs temporarily restoring border controls in the Schengen area, saying Estonia must also prioritize security over free movement slogans.

In a social media post on Saturday, Kõlvart pointed to Spain's Ceuta migration crisis as a warning of how quickly border pressures can escalate. He said decisions by authorities and courts had contributed to a situation where tens of thousands of people entered Europe within a short period.

"We can speculate about how much of this happened unintentionally and to what extent someone from the outside deliberately contributed to it, but in any case, it showed how easily such a crisis can emerge and escalate," he said, adding that migration pressure has also been used as a hybrid tactic against Europe.

Kõlvart said these recent events also serve as a reminder that in a crisis, every country must first look after its own interests. He cited Italy's temporary restoration of border controls with Spain as an example.

"Estonia, too, must also put its own interests first and prioritize its own security," he stressed.

The opposition party chair criticized Prime Minister Kristen Michal's (Reform) recent statement that free movement in Europe is a top priority and that temporarily reinstating Schengen border controls is not in Estonia's interests, calling the stance a slogan disconnected from reality.

"Free movement does not outweigh the need to mitigate the security threats Europe is currently facing," Kõlvart said.

'Estonia isn't prepared for this'

He also dismissed the prime minister's calls to hold those organizing the migration accountable as just rhetoric, saying things have already spiraled out of control and the damage has already been done in Spain.

"Unfortunately, we have to acknowledge that Estonia currently isn't prepared for migration crises like this either," Kõlvart said, warning that even a crisis a fraction of that size would be catastrophic for Estonia.

"This does not mean that everyone should fend for themselves in difficult times or that no one should help an EU member state in need," he continued. "Of course we must help Spain, but Spain itself must also take appropriate steps toward resolving this crisis, and take steps to prevent it from happening again."

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform). Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Kõlvart said the issue cannot be addressed by allowing problems to spread across Europe. While acknowledging that many migrants who arrived in Spain have since left, he said guarantees are needed that further migration waves will not follow.

"Until then, temporarily restoring border controls is a necessary and justified step," he concluded.

PM supports Spain, rejects border controls

Approximately 60,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco this week. As of Friday evening, more than 48,000 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco, Spanish officials said.

The influx comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish enclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Michal signed a joint letter with 21 other member states addressed to the EU's top leaders on Saturday calling for "an immediate and coordinated European response."

Responding to comments from opposition Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu, the prime minister also pushed back on the suggestion that suspending free movement within the EU's Schengen area would be justified in such a critical situation.

Calling the Schengen area a "great value," Michal wrote on social media that establishing new internal borders within it is in no way in Estonia's interests.

"None of us wants to return to a time when traveling overland to Central Europe meant passing through more than five cumbersome border checks," he said.

World.title: Gallery: Setos elect new leader at one-day Seto Kingdom
World.content:
Thousands gathered in Mikitamäe for Seto Kingdom Day on Saturday, where local culture advocate Ingrit Kala was elected the next ülembsootska, or leader of the Seto people.

Now in its 33rd year, the annual Seto Kingdom Day in Southeastern Estonia returned to Mikitamäe on Saturday, where sprawling grounds at the heart of the village were packed with celebrations, contests and showcases of the Seto language, food, culture, history and people.

The event culminated with the direct election of a new ülembsootska, chief regent of the Seto god-king Peko and ceremonial leader of the Seto people.

Thousands of people took part, lining up in front of their preferred candidate and gripping a rope extending from each to cast their vote.

Kala defeated fellow candidate and former nuursootska, or youth regent, Rain Oper, by a margin of several hundred supporters.

Succeeding Jalmar Vabarna, Kala will be joined in her role as leader of the Setos for the year by returning nuursootska Maria Grünberg, who was elected by children and teens the day before.

The 33rd Seto Kingdom Day took place in Mikitamäe on Saturday. August 1, 2026. Source: Leevi Lillemäe/ERR

"You have to be there for your own people, of course, and when you are invited somewhere, you go and bring them your blessing," said Kala, noting that it's important to work beyond the Seto community as well, to boost their visibility.

Kala added that developing and preserving the local Seto language would be one of her priorities as ülembsootska, noting that fewer people speak it today.

"Especially for young people, so that the Seto language doesn't disappear completely," she emphasized.

'There's always something'

Local resident Signe said Seto Kingdom Day brings together not just Setos, but those who feel connected to the Seto identity as well.

"I haven't lived here long — this is now my second year living in Setomaa," she said, adding that she had followed her heart to the region.

For Signe, one of the most important parts of the annual celebration is that it brings people together, reconnecting familiar faces and giving them a chance to catch up.

"There's always something," she added. "It's the little things that make it a wonderful day."

World.title: Warning signs now required before mobile speed cameras in Estonia
World.content:
Police in Estonia must now post warning signs before mobile speed cameras, even as officials disagree on what happens if a sign is blown over or removed.

Legislative amendments that took effect on August 1 require police to post warning signs 150–300 meters ahead of mobile speed cameras in town and 300–600 meters ahead of them on highways.

Taavi Kirss, head of traffic enforcement at the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), said officers will post signs as required and document their locations before starting speed enforcement.

"Everything depends on where we can carry out speed enforcement," Kirss said. "Where we can position ourselves and where the mobile speed camera can be placed. From there, we can determine where the warning sign can be placed."

Police record when signs are installed but cannot monitor them continuously. If one is blown over by wind or removed by someone, the officer operating the camera may not even know.

According to Kirss, however, drivers would still be required to pay any resulting fine.

"We have installed the sign as prescribed by law; we've done everything required on our end," he said.

The Interior Ministry is less certain, and expects a number of legal challenges until a court ruling settles the matter. Legal adviser Rina Sillandi said disputes would likely have to be resolved based on the evidence in each case.

"Unfortunately, it's difficult to say how this will end up working in practice," Sillandi said.

Attorney: New signs are unnecessary

Attorney Indrek Sirk said documenting when signs are installed and removed should reduce disputes, especially since mobile speed checks are typically conducted for short periods.

Nonetheless, he called the new requirement unnecessary.

"This was a propaganda measure," Sirk said, noting that some people will certainly like to see police powers limited in certain areas. "But generally speaking, I see no benefit whatsoever, for either the rule of law or traffic safety, in posting these road signs."

Mobile speed cameras have been vandalized three times this year, with offenders liable for the damage. Each repair has cost €20,000.

World.title: Schengen Area must be preserved, says Estonia's PM
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) has said the European Union must jointly act on migration after the crisis in Spain this week and that the Schengen free movement area must be preserved.

Approximately 60,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco this week. As of Friday evening, more than 48,000 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco, Spanish officials said.

The influx comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish enclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Michal signed a joint letter with 21 other member states addressed to the EU's top leaders on Saturday calling for "an immediate and coordinated European response."

"We cannot allow uncontrolled mass crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration or other hybrid threats to create the perception that illegal entry into the European Union is possible. That a migrant's illegal entry can turn into legal stay," the statement says.

It added that ministers should consider enhanced support from the EU's border force, Frontex, and "the effectiveness of EU cooperation with Morocco."

Estonia, together with 21 other Member States, calls on @eucopresident, @vonderleyen, and @MichealMartinTD to take immediate action to jointly support Spain in restoring effective control of the EU's external border.



Europe must respond with unity to uncontrolled mass crossings,… pic.twitter.com/RxMdi8zBKh — Kristen Michal (@KristenMichalPM) August 1, 2026

The letter was signed by representatives from Italy, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Sweden.

Schengen Area 'must be preserved'

He also responded to comments from the chairman of the opposition party Isamaa, Urmas Reinsalu, who said suspending the Schengen free movement zone would be justified in such a critical situation, as Italy temporarily did with Spain earlier this week.

Writing on social media, Michal said: "The creation of new internal borders within the Schengen Area is in no way in the interests of Estonia or Estonians. None of us wants to return to a time when travelling overland to Central Europe meant passing through more than five cumbersome border checks."

Michal stressed that Estonia treats every illegal border crossing with the "utmost seriousness" and is already helping other countries, such as Latvia, with their border issues.

"Those who organize such migration will be punished, and those who arrive in Estonia illegally will be detained and sent back to the countries they came from," he wrote.

"The Schengen Area is a great value that must be preserved."

'Full solidarity with Spain'

Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200). Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

While other countries took to social media to criticize Spain on Friday, Estonia's Minister of Foreign Affairs sent a message of solidarity.

"The developments in Ceuta are deeply concerning. Estonia stands in full solidarity with Spain as it faces unprecedented migration pressure," Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) wrote on social media.

"Spain has both the right and the responsibility to protect its borders – and the European Union's external border. No one has the right to enter the European Union without abiding by our common rules. Respect for those rules is essential to safeguarding the integrity of the Schengen Area," he continued.

World.title: Police will not control queue 'place buying' at Narva border
World.content:
The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) and the Ministry of Interior are not planning to crack down on people selling places in the queue at the Narva border crossing as wait times increase due to summer tourism to Russia.

The Ministry of the Interior and the PPA said they are aware that places in the queue are being sold around the Narva border crossing, Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) acknowledged in response to a question submitted by MP Aleksandr Tsaplõgin (Centre Party).

Queues at Estonia's land borders increase considerably in the summer as Russians living abroad and international tourists visit Russia. Flights from Europe were suspended following the start of the full-scale invasion, and Finland closed its borders after migration pressure several years ago. Estonia has also reduced the operational hours at the border to 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

Taro noted that the queue forms in a public space and that there are no regulations governing the line. "The PPA monitors the situation from the perspective of public order and safety. If violations or conflicts arise, the police intervene," he said.

The minister confirmed that the police assess every report indicating possible organized crime. "If specific cases contain indications of threats, extortion or other criminal activity, they are investigated and, if necessary, proceedings are initiated. It has not been confirmed that this involves a criminal group," he noted.

Minister of the Interior Igor Taro. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

The police have received reports concerning the area around the Narva border crossing, but they do not amount statistically to the volume or pattern that would indicate a widespread, systematic wave of violence or extortion.

"Reports involving threats, the risk of violence or damage to property are reviewed and, where necessary, misdemeanor or criminal proceedings are initiated if the legal grounds are met," Taro said.

In 2025, the police received 46 reports that places in the queue were being sold at Peetri Square in Narva. This year, they have received 16 such reports. Last year, there were 62 reports of public order violations, while this year the number stands at 17," the minister said.

"At the same time, it cannot be said that all of these reports are related to the border queue. Over the past two years, seven offense reports have been filed. In two cases, criminal offenses involving either theft or causing bodily injury were reported, while the remaining five involved misdemeanors, including damaging another person's property, consuming alcohol in a public place, or disobeying or insulting officials."

No proceedings have been initiated on the basis of reports about selling places in the queue. The situations have been resolved by Narva police officers, and those selling places in the queue have been removed from the line, Taro added.

Peetri plats in 2024. Source: Jenny Va / ERR

'Avoid travelling to Russia'

Asked why, despite the well-known problem, there is no permanent police presence or regular patrols near the border crossing to prevent unlawful activity, Taro replied that the law does not assign the police the task of organizing the queue of pedestrians crossing the border in a public space.

"However, the police are responsible for maintaining public order. Around the Narva border crossing, patrols and police presence are deployed on a risk-based basis where there is a greater threat to public order or security. Maintaining a permanent stationary police presence wherever a queue forms is neither practical nor proportionate. If conflicts or the threat of violence arise, people can call 112, and the police will respond," the minister said.

Tsaplõgin also asked what specific measures the Ministry of the Interior intends to take to stop the illegal sale of queue places.

"The PPA will continue to maintain public order through risk-based patrols and by responding to specific incidents. People are continually reminded of the complexity of crossing the border and the need to take into account long waiting times, restrictions and unexpected changes to border crossing procedures," Taro said.

Adding: "As a representative of the government, I support the recommendation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and likewise advise people to avoid travelling to Russia altogether!"

World.title: Three drones target northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the cities of Sulaimaniyah and Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Sunday before they were shot down without causing any casualties.

According to reports, two drones entered the skies over Sulaimaniyah. One of the two drones resulted in a fire that was eventually extinguished.

In Erbil, the C-RAM air defense system destroyed a drone early this morning without causing any damage.

These strikes follow the unexpected 72-hour pullout of US, British, French, and German forces from Erbil International Airport, which included hundreds of troops and heavy air defense equipment.

US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have departed from Erbil in the past few days, heading toward neighboring countries.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

The international coalition’s air defense systems in Erbil intercepted several earlier drones targeting the US consulate and its associated logistics base.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: Iraq forms security committee to prevent attacks against neighboring states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, chaired an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss security developments in the region.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the need to prevent any violation or threat emerging from Iraqi land toward neighboring nations, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister directed the establishment of a joint security committee to address current challenges and to follow deterrent procedures to prevent attacks or potential violations against neighboring countries.

Al-Zaidi also directed Iraqi security forces to enhance stability, protect sovereignty, and maintain good neighborly relations.

The meeting addressed the Iraqi army’s readiness to counter any attempt to strike neighboring nations, as well as Iraq’s unwavering commitment to prevent the use of its territory to launch attacks against other countries.

The formation of a joint security committee is part of Iraq’s responsibility to preserve national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.

The decision to form this committee follows substantial regional triggering events in recent days.

The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated attacks on targets in several Iraqi provinces. The alliance declared that these were retaliation strikes in response to drone and missile assaults on regional oil infrastructure and military targets.

Prior to the security meeting, Jordan and Syria cautioned Baghdad about Iran-backed armed groups operating in Iraq, warning that cross-border threats would not go unnoticed.

World.title: Iraqi court recovers IQD 20 billion in corruption and money laundering cases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Rusafa Investigative Court, which specializes in integrity and money laundering cases, has recovered 20 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $15.3 million) linked to financial corruption, administrative misconduct, and fraud, the country’s judiciary announced on Sunday.

In a statement, the judiciary’s media office said the recovered funds were tied to investigations involving financial and administrative corruption as well as financial fraud.

The court said the recovery forms part of ongoing legal efforts to pursue individuals accused of using illegal methods to obtain profits at the expense of public funds.

Authorities stressed that legal proceedings against those involved remain underway, reaffirming their commitment to combating corruption and protecting state resources.

The judiciary did not disclose additional details regarding the individuals or entities involved, nor did it specify when the alleged offenses occurred.

World.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges Americans to leave the Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Embassy in Baghdad and the US Consulate General in Erbil advised American citizens on Saturday to leave the Middle East as tensions in the region remained high.

The US mission said in a statement that due to heightened tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

The mission added that Americans presently in the Middle East should exercise extreme caution and alertness and be prepared for flight cancellations, frequent airspace closures, and possible travel difficulties.

Some regional airlines have postponed the restart of previously scheduled flights, while others have cancelled some routes.

Americans in the region are advised to consider departing or to be ready to leave if tensions escalate.

In a statement, the US Embassy in Baghdad advised that those who choose to travel to or from the region should closely monitor updates regarding airport and airline operations.

US diplomatic installations, especially those outside the Middle East, have been attacked. Iran and pro-Iran groups may attack additional US interests abroad or at areas connected with the US and Americans across the world, such as US corporations and institutions, according to the statement.

The Iranian leadership is unpredictable, as seen by recent moves to strike regions without notice, as well as to expand assaults to previously untargeted territories such as Egypt, according to the US Embassy in Iraq.

The US Embassy advised Americans to remain vigilant, as the absence of past attacks on US interests or businesses in a country does not ensure their safety.

World.title: Iraq, NATO agree to open mission office in Baghdad, expand security cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews,com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi and the commander of the NATO Mission Iraq (NMI), Lt. Gen. Ramon Armada, agreed on Sunday to open a NATO mission office in Baghdad while reaffirming continued cooperation on military training, cybersecurity, and strategic security partnerships.

According to a statement from al-Aboudi’s media office, cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the two officials held talks via video conference to discuss regional security developments and NATO’s ongoing support for Iraq’s armed forces.

During the discussion, both sides stressed the importance of reducing regional tensions and resolving recurring crises through dialogue and diplomatic channels. They also reviewed mechanisms for continuing NATO assistance in the areas of military training, advisory support, intelligence sharing, and capacity building.

A key outcome of the meeting was an agreement to establish a NATO Mission office in Baghdad, further strengthening coordination between the alliance and Iraqi security institutions.

Al-Aboudi said NATO’s role in Iraq remains focused on non-combat activities, including military advisory services, training, capacity building, cybersecurity support, and cooperation in artificial intelligence. He added that Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government is pursuing a policy of engagement with friendly and neighboring countries to advance development, investment, and mutually beneficial partnerships.

For his part, Armada reaffirmed that NATO’s advisory and training mission is committed to helping develop the capabilities of Iraq’s armed forces to address future security challenges. He said the alliance remains committed to supporting Iraq in line with the priorities established by the Iraqi government.

World.title: Zaidi threatens to resign as Coordination Framework divided over response to Saudi strikes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reportedly threatened to resign during a recent meeting of the Coordination Framework amid deep divisions over how Iraq should respond to recent Saudi military strikes, according to a report published Sunday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada.

Citing political sources, the newspaper said the prime minister’s remarks came during a tense meeting that exposed growing disagreements among senior Shiite leaders over security policy, the role of armed factions, and Baghdad’s handling of escalating regional tensions.

According to the report, the meeting became increasingly heated after intelligence was presented alleging that the armed group Saraya Awliya al-Dam was preparing to launch an attack against Jordan from Iraqi territory. The sources said Amman had warned Baghdad it would respond to any attack originating from Iraq, further intensifying the debate.

The report claims the dispute centered on whether Iraq should adhere to the government’s official position or allow individual armed factions to respond independently to the recent Saudi strikes. While most Coordination Framework leaders reportedly backed the government’s approach, one influential figure with ties to Saraya Awliya al-Dam insisted on carrying out a unilateral response.

Al-Mada reported that armed factions have given the government until next Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia. According to the sources, they warned that if Baghdad fails to act, they may launch their own response.

The newspaper also reported that the escalating dispute prompted al-Zaidi to again raise the possibility of resigning, marking what would be the second time he has reportedly made such a threat since taking office. According to the report, he previously suggested stepping down if his anti-corruption agenda failed.

The sources further claimed that the prime minister is facing mounting political pressure, including concerns about his personal security, although no official statements have confirmed those assertions.

The report also focused on the investigation into drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, stating that seven Iraqi-Saudi security meetings, with U.S. participation in some sessions, have been held over the past two months.

According to Al-Mada’s sources, the investigations have not produced conclusive evidence proving that the attacks originated from Iraqi territory, despite Saudi accusations.

The report said several scenarios remain under discussion, including the possibility that Iraqi armed factions were responsible, that Houthi operatives present in Iraq facilitated the attacks, or alternative theories promoted by some factions alleging Israeli activity in Iraq’s southern desert regions.

According to the newspaper, the ongoing crisis led al-Zaidi to cancel a planned visit to Saudi Arabia, which Iraqi officials reportedly viewed as an opportunity to attract much-needed Saudi investment at a time when Iraq faces mounting financial pressures.

The report also said armed factions have urged the prime minister to suspend efforts to bring all weapons under state control, arguing that the recent Saudi strikes have fundamentally altered the security landscape.

Al-Mada also reported that discussions during the meeting touched on the role of Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Faleh al-Fayyadh during the recent U.S.-Saudi strikes that targeted PMF facilities.

According to the newspaper’s sources, claims circulated that al-Zaidi had warned al-Fayyadh upon returning from Turkey that PMF sites could be targeted, and that evacuation efforts were delayed. However, other participants reportedly dismissed those claims, suggesting they reflected internal political disputes rather than established facts.

The Iraqi government has previously denied having prior knowledge of the U.S.-Saudi strikes. Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad neither approved nor was informed in advance of the attacks.

However, U.S. President Donald Trump later told Fox News that the strikes had been coordinated with the Iraqi government, presenting an account that differs from Baghdad’s official position.

World.title: Zaidi’s failed raid on Nujaba base exposes challenges in disarmament push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A failed security operation targeting a facility belonging to the Iran-aligned Harakat al-Nujaba movement has underscored the challenges facing the Iraqi government as it seeks to bring all armed groups under state control before the end of September.

According to a report published by Al-Monitor, a joint Iraqi force attempted to search a Harakat al-Nujaba compound in Baghdad’s Jurf al-Naddaf district on July 24 after receiving intelligence suggesting the site contained missiles and drones. However, the operation ended without the facility being searched after armed members of the group confronted government forces.

The report, citing Iraqi security officials, said the operation involved Baghdad Operations Command, the Federal Police, and the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Security Directorate. Shortly after arriving at the compound, commanders affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba reportedly ordered their fighters to prevent security personnel from entering. Armed members of the group then surrounded the government force and fired warning shots into the air, forcing the operation to halt.

According to the officials, the PMF leadership subsequently instructed its personnel to withdraw, stating they had not been informed that the target was a facility affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba. Army units involved in the operation later received similar withdrawal orders. No casualties were reported, and neither the government nor the armed group publicly disclosed details of the incident at the time.

The incident comes as Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has pledged to ensure that all weapons in Iraq are brought under state control by September 30, the scheduled end of the U.S.-led coalition’s military mission in the country.

Al-Monitor described the failed operation as the first significant field test of the government’s commitment to enforcing that pledge. While previous administrations also announced plans to limit weapons to state institutions, implementation has remained difficult due to the political and military influence of several armed factions.

Hayder al-Shakeri, a researcher with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, told Al-Monitor that although Baghdad has increasingly relied on restructuring security institutions and applying political and financial pressure on armed groups, the Jurf al-Naddaf operation demonstrated the limits of the state’s authority when confronted directly.

“If the government cannot enforce its decisions against a single armed faction, or fails to follow through with legal and political accountability, it suggests that these groups still retain an effective veto over certain state actions,” Al-Shakeri was quoted as saying.

The report noted that not all Iran-aligned factions share the same position regarding government efforts to centralize weapons under state control.

Some groups, including Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have become increasingly integrated into Iraq’s political and economic systems, potentially reducing their willingness to engage in direct confrontation. Others—including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada—continue to oppose any move that would place their military capabilities under full government authority.

Political analyst Muhannad al-Ghazi told Al-Monitor that these factions view their weapons through an ideological lens, making voluntary disarmament highly unlikely. He argued that targeting isolated weapons caches without addressing broader military infrastructure would have only a limited impact.

The reported confrontation occurred amid heightened regional tensions following Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s recent visit to Washington, where Iraq and the United States announced a strategic economic partnership.

According to Al-Monitor, several Iran-backed factions criticized the visit, warning against what they described as replacing “military occupation” with “economic occupation” through expanded U.S. investment in Iraq.

The report also linked the incident to broader regional developments, including recent drone attacks and cross-border military operations that have intensified pressure on Baghdad’s efforts to assert control over its territory.

Al-Monitor concluded that the government’s September 30 target for fully disarming armed factions appears increasingly difficult to achieve given current realities.

Instead, analysts cited by the publication believe Baghdad may focus on more gradual measures, including relocating some weapons, closing selected facilities, and increasing political and financial pressure on groups willing to cooperate, while avoiding direct confrontation with the most heavily armed factions.

The report suggested that the ultimate success of Iraq’s disarmament strategy may depend not only on domestic enforcement but also on broader regional dynamics, particularly relations between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Jordan threatens to strike Iranian militias in Iraq if they launched attacks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Amman has publicly warned Iraq that it will launch military operations against Iran-backed militias if they attack Jordan.

The warning comes after a rapid increase in regional violence, including recent interceptions of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones over Jordanian airspace, which targeted US installations.

An official Jordanian source told Al-Arabiya News that Jordan provided Iraq with precise intelligence indicating that pro-Iran militants are planning to strike Jordanian territory.

Jordan has publicly said that it expects the Iraqi government to take quick and effective measures to curb these armed groups.

Jordanian sources identify front organizations such as Awliya al-Dam as key players in these border-threatening actions.

The warning represents a strong change in Jordan’s defensive stance in the face of rising tensions between the United States and Iran.

Jordan harbors critical Western military installations, such as the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, which have become active targets for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its allies in the region.

Jordan emphasized that, while it aims to avoid regional escalation, it considers national sovereignty and border security to be inviolable priorities.

World.title: Ramlila body asks 'Ramayana' makers to hold special screening before release, warns of protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Shri Ramlila Mahasangh has asked the makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana to hold a special preview screening for its representatives before the film's worldwide theatrical release, warning that it will stage protests if the request is not accepted.

In a letter addressed to director Nitesh Tiwari and the film's production company, Shri Ramlila Mahasangh president Arjun Kumar sought a screening of the film ahead of its Diwali 2026 release in India and overseas to ensure it does not contain scenes that could hurt Hindu sentiments.

The demand comes in the backdrop of the controversy surrounding the 2023 film Adipurush, which drew criticism over its depiction of characters and settings from the Hindu epic.

Recalling the earlier controversy, Kumar said members of the Sanatan community and those associated with traditional Ramlila performances had objected to several aspects of Adipurush, including "the depiction of Lanka in black instead of gold, and the portrayal of Ravana and his army in a manner that did not align with traditional beliefs."

"According to information received by the Mahasangh, Ramayana may also contain certain scenes that could hurt the sentiments of Hindus living in India and abroad.





In light of this, the organisation has requested a special preview screening to ensure that any potentially objectionable scenes or dialogues are identified and removed prior to release," Kumar said in a press note.

He also warned that if the filmmakers do not agree to the request, the Shri Ramlila Mahasangh, along with various Hindu organisations, will stage protests and demonstrations outside cinema halls in Delhi and other states.

I have no further information," he said.A supporter of Yadav who was present said he instinctively put his hand in front of the MP as the knife was swung, causing the blade to graze his finger.The situation descended into a melee, with people falling and piling on top of one another.The convenor also alleged that Delhi Police personnel present did not intervene to protect Yadav and instead focused on taking the alleged attackers away. "I tried to help Pappu Yadav escape the scene. The police seemed to be shielding the goons... Not a single policeman stepped forward to help Pappu Yadav escape. When the assault was taking place, they focused solely on saving the goons and whisked them away from the scene. We don't know where they took them," he alleged."These people had come to stage a 'Prayagraj Part Two' â they came to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident today," the convenor said, referring to the 2023 killing of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed and his brother in Prayagraj while they were in police custody.The convenor said he had met the DCP earlier in the day and submitted a formal complaint warning that the MP was arriving and had been receiving constant threats on social media. "Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here, and even they were merely protecting the goons," he alleged.He further alleged that several people had been positioned behind the media cameras before the incident. "There were people hiding behind the cameras, three or four of them. Suddenly, someone pulled out a knife, another a slipper... The MP was the target, no one else," he said.According to people present at the scene, the confrontation began after some men allegedly accused Yadav of insulting Sanatan Dharma. The men argued with him before one of them removed a slipper and attempted to throw it. Yadav's supporters then intervened, leading to a scuffle.Yadav and his supporters have alleged the men were carrying knives and had intentions to kill him. The Delhi Police have not yet issued an official statement on the incident.Yadav himself alleged in a later statementthat the confrontation was an attempt on his life and linked it to threats against his family.âI came here because last night, they went to my childrenâs home. Now, you are trying to intimidate my children too; that wonât happen,â Yadav said. âI was with the press, and a conversation was underway. Amid that, there was an attempt to kill me.âHe alleged that some of those involved were calling for him to be killed, adding, âSome âBabaâ was saying, âBurn him alive,â while others were saying, âKill him.â If people hadnât been here, I would have been finished.âYadav also connected the confrontation to the ongoing controversy over alleged discrepancies involving offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.âI havenât said anything. I only asked Champat Rai or Giri Ji, where did the 200 kg of silver go? Where did the gold go?â he said.On security concerns, Yadav said he had repeatedly sought protection. âThe Delhi Police is quite capable. I have been demanding security for a long time now. What crime have I committed?â he said.The confrontation comes days after Yadav was involved in a political controversy over a protest by opposition MPs concerning alleged theft of offerings made at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Yadav, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad and other opposition parliamentarians staged a demonstration in Parliament premises in which they enacted a skit depicting the alleged theft of temple offerings.Yadav wore saffron during the protest and portrayed a temple priest who allegedly took offerings from a donation box. The demonstration drew criticism from seers and others, who accused the MPs of insulting Sanatan Dharma.

World.title: Assam floods: 82 dead, 1.78 lakh affected as relief efforts intensify - key points
World.content:
Assam continued to grapple with the aftermath of devastating floods on Sunday, with the death toll remaining at 82 and nearly 1.78 lakh people still affected across seven districts.

Although floodwaters have begun to recede in some areas, thousands remain displaced, agricultural land is submerged, and the state government has intensified relief, rehabilitation and long-term mitigation efforts.

According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the flood situation has improved slightly, with the number of affected people declining from over 1.92 lakh to 1.78 lakh. However, 349 villages across Golaghat, Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, Bajali, Dhemaji and Sonitpur districts remain affected.

Charaideo is the worst-hit district, with more than 75,000 people affected, followed by over 58,000 in Sivasagar. Nearly 15,060 hectares of crop area remain submerged, while thousands of livestock have been affected or washed away.

Relief and rescue under way

A total of 44 relief camps are currently sheltering around 15,000 displaced people, while another 17 relief distribution centres are providing assistance to more than 5,500 residents.





The state government has directed district administrations to expedite the identification of affected families so that financial assistance can begin from August 3.

Villagers rescue over 1,000 people in Sivasagar

One of the most remarkable rescue stories emerged from the Nepali Khuti area in Sivasagar district, where local villagers used six country-made boats to rescue more than 1,000 people from five villages after floodwaters rose rapidly on July 19.

Residents said families were trapped on rooftops, elevated platforms and trees as water levels surged.

The volunteer rescuers continued operations through the night despite having little food or water, ferrying stranded villagers to safer areas.

CM reviews flood-hit districts and compensation plans

Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma began a tour of the worst-hit districts on Sunday to oversee relief operations and prepare for a comprehensive damage assessment exercise scheduled to begin on August 9.

The government has also directed officials to ensure uninterrupted distribution of relief kits, assess damage to educational institutions before schools reopen on August 10, and prepare restoration plans for damaged Namghars (Vaishnavite prayer centres).

IIT-Guwahati to be engaged for Brahmaputra erosion solution

During his visit to erosion-hit areas of Dibrugarh district, including Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria, Sarma announced that the state government will engage experts from IIT-Guwahati to develop a long-term solution to the Brahmaputra riverâs erosion problem.

Calling riverbank erosion one of Assamâs biggest geographical challenges, the chief minister said the state loses valuable land every year and that modern technology would be used to strengthen vulnerable riverbanks.

The proposed IIT initiative will complement the governmentâs planned Rs 90 crore erosion mitigation project.

Agriculture rehabilitation begins

Agriculture minister Pijush Hazarika visited Charaideo district on Sunday to review post-flood rehabilitation measures and launched community paddy nurseries and seedling distribution programmes for flood-affected farmers.

The government said quality seedlings and other assistance would be provided to ensure cultivation resumes without delay during the current agricultural season.

Aid pours in from NGOs, celebrities and political organisations

Support for flood-hit communities has continued to grow across Assam.

Actor Randeep Hooda joined a relief drive organised by Global Sikhs in Sivasagar district, distributing essential supplies and serving food through langar for affected families. He warned that prolonged waterlogging and mud-filled homes could trigger disease outbreaks and urged people across the country to contribute to relief efforts.

The Lok Janshakti Party (Ramvilas) has also launched a large-scale relief operation in Sivasagar, distributing food and essential supplies and announcing plans to feed up to 15,000 people daily for 10 days, along with setting up medical camps.

Centre sanctions Rs 379 crore for flood relief

The Centre has approved Rs 379.35 crore under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for Assamâs flood response. Sarma thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for extending assistance and for deploying Inter-Ministerial Central Teams to support relief and rehabilitation planning.

Reliance Foundation has also contributed Rs 21 crore to the Chief Ministerâs Relief Fund for flood relief and rehabilitation efforts.

While water levels have started falling in parts of the state, the crisis is far from over. Thousands remain displaced, farmland continues to lie under water, and many families face the difficult task of rebuilding homes and livelihoods. Alongside immediate relief operations, the government is now focusing on compensation, agricultural recovery and long-term measures to address the recurring twin challenges of floods and Brahmaputra erosion.

World.title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday criticised the ban on former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasinaâs Awami League party, calling it a "move against democracyâ and expressing uncertainty over Hasinaâs return to the country.

âNo political party should be banned. The manner in which Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy. I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible,â Nasreen told reporters at a press conference in Kolkata.

Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests.

The interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after the fall of the Awami League administration, banned the party in May 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.

Meanwhile, Nasreen alleged that several Awami League workers had been tortured and killed during Sheikh Hasinaâs exile and expressed uncertainty over whether the former prime minister would be able to return to Bangladesh.

âMany Awami League workers were tortured and murdered. Sheikh Hasina wants to return, but I do not know whether that will be possible.





But no one wants me to go back,â she said.

Nasreen also criticised Jamaat-e-Islami, now Bangladesh's principal opposition party, accusing it of opposing womenâs equality and seeking the imposition of Sharia law.

âNow we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an opposition party. It is against womenâs equality, and they want Sharia rule. If that happens, no minority will survive. Bangladesh is moving towards darkness. No one is trying to civilise Bangladesh.

The government is only trying to remain in power,â she added.

The 63-year-old author further claimed that âhatred against Hindusâ was being spread in some madrasas and mosques in Bangladesh.

âIn many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus,â Nasreen remarked.

Nasreen backs Uniform Civil Code , calls it necessary for women's equality

Turning to the issue of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Nasreen said she had been advocating for such a law for the past 40 years and described it as essential in any âcivilised countryâ.

âI have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country,â she remarked.

She claimed that religious laws continued to affect womenâs rights in Bangladesh, alleging that Hindu women in the country lacked adequate legal protections, including the right to divorce.

âIn Bangladesh, Hindu girls have no rights; they do not even have the right to divorce. Due to religious laws, women are suffering.

Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more,â she alleged.

In July, the BJP-led West Bengal government constituted a nine-member expert committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai to examine and finalise a draft UCC for the state. The state government plans to introduce the legislation during the upcoming August Assembly session.

She was forced to leave the city in 2007 following protests over her writings and memoir Dwikhandito (Split into Two), published in 2003.

World.title: 'If India is so great, why settle in Dubai?' Raj Thackeray targets Vivek Oberoi, R Madhavan
World.content:
MNS chief

on Sunday launched a sharp attack on industrialists and public figures who praise Prime Minister

and the BJP government while choosing to live abroad, questioning their claims that India had improved significantly under the current administration. Speaking at the 20th anniversary rally of the Maharashtra Navnirman Vidyarthi Sena in Mumbai, Thackeray cited actors

and R Madhavan as examples and linked their decisions to what he described as growing frustration among the country's youth.

Claiming that the government had itself acknowledged in Parliament that entrepreneurs were leaving India, Thackeray argued that many of those who publicly endorse the government's narrative were unwilling to build their own lives in the country.

"Vivek Oberoi, who played Modi's role in the movie on Modi's life, lives in Dubai. R. Madhavan, who goes on about how everything became great during Modi's time and how the country changed, moves to Dubai with his family.

If you think Modi has made everything so great, then why are you settling abroad? These people will come here to work in government-sponsored films and then go back to Dubai," he said.

He added that the trend was not limited to actors, saying, "Industrialists are going abroad."

Thackeray said the migration of entrepreneurs and young professionals reflected a deeper crisis of confidence, arguing that Indian cities had failed to provide the quality of life that many young people expected.





"This government made a big fuss about 'Smart Cities.' Where are those Smart Cities? Not a single city here is proper. Today, kids are going abroad. Why? Because they don't feel like living here. The cities are ruined; there's no place to take children out. Abroad, there are excellent roads, fields, gardens, cleanliness, sports complexes, everything. Because of all this, these kids feel like going abroad and settling there.

And we feel nothing about it?" he said.

The MNS chief also weighed in on Prime Minister Modi's remarks condemning abusive language directed at him and his mother, saying he agreed that such language was unacceptable but accused the BJP of nurturing a culture of online abuse.

"The language used against him was indeed inappropriate. No one should use such language about anyone. It was wrong. But tell this to your people too.

Since 2012, the troll army that your party has nurtured trolls everyone, from Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, to Indira Gandhi, to all of us including me, in the filthiest ways. Today, if artists in Maharashtra take a stand against the government, they get trolled.

Tell your people about all this sometime. You reap what you sow," he said.

He continued, "The Prime Minister said wrong things were said about his mother. That was indeed wrong. Such things shouldn't happen. But tell your party people that others have mothers too. Tell the trolls you've nurtured. You say, 'The kids have been forgiven.' But who will apologize for what your people did? Those who ordered lathis on students, those who split students' heads open, who will they ever apologize?"

Addressing student activists, Thackeray argued that recent protests should not be viewed merely through the lens of the NEET examination controversy.

He said the unrest reflected wider concerns over unemployment, privatisation, poor infrastructure, corruption and the lack of opportunities.

"The protests that happened weren't just because of the NEET exam chaos. Go beyond that and think about what's simmering in the minds of the boys and girls, the young men and women," he said, warning that further public anger could erupt if those concerns remained unaddressed.

World.title: One-year-old girl run over by car in Madivala; driver booked
World.content:
A one-year-old girl was killed after she was run over by a car in an apartment parking area at Dollars Scheme Colony near Someshwara Temple in Madivala on Saturday.

Prakash Pandey was living in the apartment with his wife and two daughters, aged six and one. He was working as a security guard in one of the flats in the apartment.

On Saturday around 12.30 p.m., Pandey was cleaning a parked vehicle. He seated his daughter near the gate. The flat owner’s son, identified as Rahil Javed, 19, allegedly sought Pandey’s help to take a parked car out from the parking area.

After the task, Pandey noticed that his daughter was missing from the spot. On checking, he allegedly found her caught under the wheels of the car that Javed drove. The child became unconscious. The family immediately rushed the girl to a hospital and was later referred to St. John’s Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her brought dead.

Based on Pandey’s complaint, the Madivala police have registered a case against the driver for causing death due to negligence and issued a notice to the accused for questioning.

World.title: Centre played a key role in State’s development: A.P. BJP spokesperson
World.content:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) State spokesperson Sheikh Baji on Sunday said the Centre had been extending significant financial and infrastructural support for the development of Andhra Pradesh.

Mr. Baji stated that the Centre had released thousands of crores of rupees for the completion of the Polavaram national project and had also extended financial support for the development of Amaravati as the State capital.

According to him, the Centre had been supporting the expansion of highways, railway projects, ports, airports, industrial corridors, educational institutions and healthcare infrastructure in the State. He said initiatives such as the establishment of the South Coast Railway Zone with Visakhapatnam as its headquarters and assistance for the development of the Bhogapuram international airport would strengthen the State's long-term growth prospects.

Mr. Baji said special financial assistance had been announced for Amaravati in the 2024–25 Union Budget and continued to support the speedy completion of the Polavaram project. He noted that around ₹10,000 crore had been allocated for railway projects in 2025–26, while ₹3,300 crore had been earmarked for the Polavaram project.

The BJP leader said Andhra Pradesh had been receiving substantial allocations through tax devolution, centrally sponsored schemes and programmes related to rural development, housing, drinking water supply, healthcare, education and employment generation.

He added that schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi, Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, Ujjwala Yojana, Swachh Bharat Mission and the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana had benefited millions of people across the State.

Mr. Baji maintained that the Centre’s initiatives such as PM Gati Shakti, Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Digital India had helped attract investments, create employment opportunities and accelerate industrial growth in Andhra Pradesh.

He called upon people to view the State's development from a broader national perspective rather than through a political lens and asserted that the Centre would continue to support Andhra Pradesh's progress.

World.title: Sharmila slams A.P. government for neglecting Godavari flood victims
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Y. S. Sharmila on Sunday slammed the TDP-led coalition government in the State for what she alleged as "showing far more interest in praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi and glorifying his leadership than in addressing the plight of the Godavari flood-affected regions.”

“The enthusiasm displayed in singing the Prime Minister’s praises is conspicuously absent when it comes to rescuing and supporting people stranded by the floods,” she posted on X.

Ms. Sharmila said that, at a time when entire villages were submerged, as the Godavari River was in spate, and additionally, residents of nearly 100 villages were living in fear for their lives, it was shameful that the government had failed to act with urgency.

“More than 20,000 people have reportedly lost their homes and livelihoods due to the floodwaters and have been displaced, yet the government has shown little concern in providing immediate rehabilitation or reassurance,” she alleged.

She said that if criticism of Prime Minister Modi can evoke strong reactions from the government, then the suffering of displaced families should also evoke the same concern.

“Have the scenes of people packing up their belongings and abandoning their villages gone unnoticed? If authorities knew flooding was imminent, why were residents not evacuated to safer areas in advance?” she questioned.

The State Congress chief demanded that the government stand by the people in the flood-affected regions until the impact of the Godavari floods subsides and undertake immediate rehabilitation measures. “Adequate food facilities must be provided in relief and rehabilitation centres and essential commodities should be distributed to affected families, she said, adding that medical services must also be made available to those suffering from health issues, with special attention given to children and pregnant women.

She also said that given that floods occur every year, the government should provide Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) packages to residents of the Polavaram submergence villages and ensure better rehabilitation in safer locations.

World.title: Slipper hurled at Pappu Yadav at presser as he defends skit on Ram temple donation theft
World.content:
A man threw a slipper at Independent MP Pappu Yadav during a press conference at his house on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after the lawmaker defended his skit inside the Parliament House complex on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple, leading to a scuffle between his supporters and the attacker.

Mr. Yadav was addressing the presser amid a row over his Friday (July 31, 2026) protest with an FIR being filed in Varanasi against him, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP from Faizabad (Ayodhya) Awadhesh Prasad for allegedly hurting religious sentiments.

While Mr. Yadav was addressing the presser, a man questioned him over his actions and alleged that the MP had insulted Lord Ram. He then threw a slipper at Mr. Yadav, and a scuffle ensued between the Purnia MP’s supporters and the attacker.

Mr. Yadav later alleged that it was an attempt on his life.

According to police sources, the alleged attacker was identified as 34-year-old Sumit, a native of Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr, who works in an iron fabrication business in Ghaziabad and has no previous criminal record.

The police source said that another man, identified as Happy, was present in an SUV parked outside Yadav’s residence when the incident occurred.

Investigators are verifying their claims and probing the motive behind the incident.

Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav, dressed in a saffron outfit, performed the skit on Friday (July 31, 2026) in the Parliament House complex along with other Opposition MPs in front of the Makar Dwar at the Parliament complex to protest the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

The MPs, including Rahul Gandhi, put money inside donation boxes, while Mr. Yadav slipped money into his pockets to symbolise the alleged theft at the Ram temple.

The BJP on Sunday (August 2, 2026) accused Mr. Gandhi and Mr. Yadav of hurting Hindu sentiments and demanded that they publicly apologise.

However, a defiant Yadav said they were protesting to protect Sanatan and will not be cowed down by any number of FIRs.

He was reacting a day after a case was filed in Varanasi on the complaint of seers against him, Mr. Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP from Faizabad (Ayodhya) Awadhesh Prasad while BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj and other leaders filed a police complaint in Delhi.

The RSS affiliate Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also attacked Mr. Gandhi and Mr. Yadav, alleging that the two leaders insulted Sanatan Dharma through the protest staged in the Parliament complex.

World.title: U.K. PM Burnham signals support for written constitution
World.content:
Britain's new Prime Minister Andy Burnham has signalled his support for a written constitution for the U.K., which unlike most countries, does not have one authoritative document.

Since entering office just two weeks ago, the former Mayor of Greater Manchester has made devolution of power to regional authorities a focus of his administration.

"In the end, I think it does start to point towards a new constitutional settlement," Mr. Burnham said of his devolution plans on the weekend.

Calling for a "new clear set of principles about how this country should be run", Mr. Burnham said there was a need for a written Constitution — something he has called for before he was Prime Minister.

"It's wrong that people are left arguing for things that are just fundamental... and the lack of a constitution disempowers places in that situation," said Mr. Burnham.

Unlike most countries around the world, Britain does not have a written Constitution, and is instead governed by a patchwork of statutes, common law judgments, and treaties.

The push for a written Constitution is fairly recent, with Labour's Gordon Brown, who was Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010, an early proponent of the overhaul.

Mr. Burnham served as a Minister in Mr. Brown's government.

A parliamentary committee considered options for codifying the Constitution in a five-year review, which concluded in 2015 that there was no clear consensus.

Any serious attempt to codify the Constitution by Mr. Burnham would be a years-long process likely requiring a major public inquiry and consultations.

Mr. Burnham on Friday (July 31, 2026) announced plans to allow regional Mayors in England to keep a share of taxes collected in their area, part of his drive to transfer power out of the highly centralised nation's capital.

The UK — comprising England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland — saw significant constitutional reforms in the late 1990s that created devolved Parliaments in Edinburgh, Cardiff and Belfast.

But England itself remains one of Europe's most centralised nations, despite the creation of some regional Mayors and other bodies in the last decade, experts say.

World.title: Police constable recruitment examination held under tight security in Mangaluru, Udupi
World.content:
The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) conducted the examination for the direct recruitment of police constables (civil) under tight security at 15 centres across Mangaluru and Udupi on Sunday. More than 6,000 candidates had registered for the exam, which was conducted between 10.30 a.m. and 12 noon.

A total of 4,022 candidates were registered to write the examination at nine centres in Mangaluru. The highest number of candidates, 686, was allotted to St. Aloysius PU College, while 504 were allotted to St. Agnes PU College. As many as 480 candidates each were allotted to Government PU College, Balmatta; Canara PU College; and Vikas PU College. Another 408 were allotted to Shree Gokarnanatheshwara PU College, 360 to Government PU College, Car Street, and 312 each to Milagres PU College and Sri Narayanaguru PU College.

According to a press note, 3,448 candidates were present and 574 were absent for the examination in Mangaluru.

In Udupi, a total of 2,367 candidates were registered to write the examination at six centres in Udupi city. Most of the candidates were from Udupi district. To help candidates, the Udupi district police had arranged free lodging facilities at Mathura Comforts Hall and the Mahalakshmi temple auditorium in Udupi town.

Apart from increasing security at the examination centres, the Udupi police had installed network signal jammers to prevent the use of electronic devices. Webcasting of all the centres was done, and the footage was viewed by officers posted at the command centre. All candidates were allowed into the centres only after a facial recognition check. CCTV cameras were installed at all the centres.

The Udupi police cautioned candidates against leaking the question paper on social media, warning of strict legal action. Those wearing religious attire had to undergo special screening and were asked to arrive at the centre two hours before the exam began. Similar instructions were issued to special candidates who came to the centre with hearing aids and cochlear implants.

World.title: DMK accuses State government of sleeping over Cauvery issue
World.content:
Former DMK Minister S. Regupathy on Sunday (August 2, 2026) accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government of remaining passive on the crucial Cauvery water dispute and criticised Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for “failing to clarify the government’s stand” on the issue.

In a statement issued in Chennai, Mr. Regupathy said that as Chief Minister, Mr. Vijay had a responsibility to explain the government’s position on vital issues such as the Cauvery dispute.

Claiming Mr. Vijay avoided interacting with the media to protect his public image, Mr. Regupathy said neither the Chief Minister nor Water Resources Minister N. Anand had spelt out the government’s stand on Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu project. He said Mr. Vijay and Mr. Anand owed the people an explanation as to whether they endorsed Electricity Minister R. Nirmalkumar’s view that there was no need to convene an all-party meeting on the issue.

Accusing the TVK Government of “sleeping over” a matter of immense importance to the State, Mr. Regupathy alleged Mr. Nirmalkumar had insulted the Opposition parties in Tamil Nadu as well as former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi through his remarks.

“While the Tamil Nadu government remains silent, the Karnataka Chief Minister is holding regular high-level meetings, meeting Union Ministers and convening all-party meetings on the issue,” he said.

Mr. Regupathy contended the Chief Minister’s silence would create the impression that Tamil Nadu was being governed by a weak administration.

“It is not only neighbouring States but even the Governor who will begin to view the Tamil Nadu government as weak. The Chief Minister’s refusal to consult political parties and his apparent rest mode during weekends have caused serious concern among farmers,” he said.

Mr. Regupathy demanded that the State government convene an all-party meeting to deliberate on the Cauvery water dispute and sought an apology from Mr. Nirmalkumar for his remarks.

Meanwhile, DMK legal wing deputy secretary I. Paranathan took strong exception to Mr. Nirmalkumar’s comments on Karunanidhi, stating that it was Karunanidhi who had secured the establishment of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal. “He has no locus standi to speak about Kalaignar,” Mr. Paranathan said.

Responding to Mr. Nirmalkumar’s contention that an all-party meeting was unnecessary because every political party had its own stand, Mr. Paranathan said it was the Chief Minister’s responsibility to build consensus among political parties on issues affecting the State.

“All Chief Ministers in the past had convened all-party meetings on matters concerning the Cauvery dispute,” he said.

World.title: Woman held for drowning nine-month-old daughter in Bairamalguda lake
World.content:
A 34-year-old woman was taken into custody after she drowned her nine-month-old daughter in Bairamalguda Lake on Sunday evening.

According to the police, the accused, Lokasani Rajeshwari, a homemaker from Injapur in Rangareddy district and a native of Bidar district in Karnataka, allegedly drowned her daughter, Anuradha, at around 6.30 p.m.

The body was shifted to the Osmania General Hospital mortuary for postmortem examination.

Police said Rajeshwari was allegedly under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. She has been taken into custody, and a case has been registered. The motive behind the incident is yet to be ascertained, and further investigation is underway.

World.title: At least 14 killed in suicide attack on Kabal police station in Swat
World.content:
The death toll from the suicide attack outside Swat’s Kabal police station on Sunday has risen to 14, police said.

Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi confirmed to Dawn that 14 people lost their lives in the blast.

Earlier, Swat’s Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain told AFP that seven people had died, which included four police officers, with 20 people injured.

According to the Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Umar Khan, the suicide bomber detonated explosives after police personnel attempted to stop and search him at the entrance of the police station.

The DPO said that the police remained on high alert. “Security forces have cordoned off the area, and an investigation is underway to collect further evidence,“ he added.

The explosion occurred near the gate of Kabal Police Station while hundreds of people were participating in a public demonstration at the nearby Kabal Chowk, against the recent wave of terrorism in the Swat Valley.

The powerful blast caused multiple casualties, prompting an immediate emergency response by police, rescue teams and local authorities.

The injured were shifted to nearby Saidu Sharif Teaching Hospital for treatment, while security personnel sealed off the area and launched a search operation.

The protest had drawn a large crowd from across the district and the attack occurred as the final speaker was addressing the crowd, triggering panic among participants. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Addressing the gathering before the blast, the speakers condemned the resurgence of terrorism in Swat and demanded that the government ensure lasting peace. They said their movement had a single agenda: the restoration of peace and the elimination of terrorism from the region.

The speakers stressed that maintaining law and order and eradicating terrorism were the state’s responsibility, warning that continued insecurity could trigger widespread public unrest, citing recent protest movements in other countries as examples of growing public frustration.

The speakers also criticised the authorities for what they described as action against peaceful citizens while terrorists continued to operate in the mountainous areas of Swat. They alleged that terrorists had openly circulated videos on social media and questioned why stronger action had not been taken against them.

“Our children deserve education, and our families deserve to live in peace,” one speaker told the gathering.

“We have witnessed years of bloodshed. Our mothers, sisters, and daughters have suffered immensely, and we do not want another generation of widows and orphans.”

Earlier in the day, an IED blast near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza injured two policemen in the provincial capital Peshawar. On July 30, a terrorist attack on a police checkpost in Hangu martyred nine policemen.

KP has seen an uptick in terrorist activity. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’s monthly security assessment, KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 terrorism related deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, representing an increase of 105 per cent.

Condemnations pour in

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the blast, expressing sorrow at the loss of life. “Terrorists cannot demoralise the nation with cowardly attacks,” Kundi was quoted as saying, as per a statement.

KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, condemning the incident, sought a report from the KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) and offered condolences to the families of the deceased.

“The elements hostile to peace will never be allowed to succeed in their nefarious intentions,” the chief minister was quoted as saying.
